item.title: Campaign Organizer Come To Nebraska Defeat Pete Ricketts Flip The Senate
item.description: Campaign Organizer- Nebraska Location and Timeline: We are hiring a full-time Campaign Organizer to begin by the end of August and continue through Election Day. The locations are Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. This will expand over the program, so if you are a Nebraskan who lives further away or willing to relocate, please still apply! Who We Are: The Outreach Team is the national engine of campaigners and organizers building a fairer, cleaner, safer, and more peaceful world. We invest in people at every level with industry-leading pay/benefits, rigorous training and support and real paths to leadership. General Overview: Neighbor, it’s your time to step up for Nebraska. We need your love for our state and its people, your skills earned from years of hard work, and your ability to connect with other Nebraskans. Frankly, it’s the only way we are going to pry back our government and economy from the billionaires who have taken over. The good news is that there are more of us than there are of them. We just need to harness our power… conversation by conversation, on every porch, corner, driveway, sidewalk, field, and farm in Nebraska. And we need you to lead the charge. Join us on behalf of the Working Class Majority Pac. We are looking for Organizers to talk to voters about Dan Osborn’s run for Senate in Nebraska’s upcoming election. If you believe that real political power is built from the ground up through deep organizing and face-to-face conversations, we want you on our team in Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. Organizers will be charged with recruiting, training, and working with a team of volunteers in key counties in Nebraska. The Organizer will start by building and recruiting a team of supporters and volunteers around canvassing. From there, Organizers will continue to engage volunteers through a series of campaign events and actions. Requirements: Valid driver's license and Insurance as well as a verifiable record of safe driving. Must be over 21 (in order to drive the rental car if needed) Must be available full-time. What You'll Do: Recruit and Train a Community of Volunteer Activists Call and text supporters and recruit them into grassroots actions. Identify new supporters and volunteers by knocking doors, gathering petitions, flyering, and conducting in-field recruitment efforts in the community and on local campuses. Run grassroots skills training to develop effective campaigners among volunteers. Keep meticulous track of a volunteer list so that no potential volunteer falls through the cracks. Represent the campaign through participation in community spaces and events, while engaging and uplifting coalition and partner organizations. Generate Campaign Actions Gather over a thousand petitions from the community in support of key campaign issues. Recruit and train volunteers to generate more petitions and volunteer engagement at events. Recruit and engage with community leaders, organizational partners, and VIPs to build meaningful relationships while generating new supporters, volunteers, and event attendees. Organize High-Volume Visibility Events Organize and execute exciting, high-visibility in-person events demonstrating support for working families in Nebraska. Educate community members about constituents around affordability and action opportunities and the urgency of continued actions. Nail 100% of all messaging and legal requirements and ensure that volunteers do the same. Manage Digital Campaign, Data Management, and Reporting Tools Demonstrate public support by recruiting volunteers to post on their own social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. Use peer-to-peer texting services and relational organizing tools to communicate with community members. Write and send timely and compelling email campaigns to recruit activists to campaign activities. Track every interaction with detailed notes in order to report numbers daily and write weekly reports on the results of the campaign. Who You Are & Keys to Success (the must-haves): To be successful in this job, you will excel in these areas: Relationship Building: You develop and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with a diverse group of local and statewide community members. You are attentive and empathetic to the communities we serve, regardless of race, ethnicity, class, gender, or ability, and can identify shared values across communities for collective growth. You can build authentic relationships through authenticity and reliability, continuously uplifting others and their goals. You are comfortable and experienced in public speaking to a group about constituents around affordability and action opportunities. Inclusive and Collaborative Leadership: You approach leadership with a "power with" mindset that recognizes the impact power hierarchies have in different settings. You can learn from others, see and hear other perspectives, and step in or step back as necessary. You are reliable and accountable, always transparent about your abilities, capacities, and expectations. You honor the time and commitments of others while inspiring them to meet goals. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion: You have a proven ability to develop meaningful connections with diverse communities, including a wide range of community organizations, community leaders, and community members. You work with the community and within the workplace to identify areas of improvement for a more equitable environment. You take continued action and efforts to improve your REI knowledge, skills, and tools. Drive to Achieve Results: You have experience accomplishing ambitious goals and getting results, even when there are obstacles. You have the experience or ability to plan backwards to meet multiple goals timely and effectively. When there are unexpected changes, you bounce back and adjust quickly, learning and improving from any mistakes. Skills and Experiences we Expect of all Outreach Team employees: Commitment to equity and justice. Experience bringing a lens of inclusivity to all of your interactions with colleagues and community members. Passion for the role that your work plays in creating change in the world. Kindness and consideration for others. Drive to work collaboratively: learning from others; stepping-in or stepping-back when needed. Transparency: comfort admitting what you do and don't know, your capacity, and abilities. Task management: Able to adapt to the evolving needs of a project. Able to tackle big-picture projects and break them down into smaller pieces. Organized and efficient: Experience or demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects or goals at once in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Acute attention to detail: Track interactions and tasks with detailed notes. Plans ahead for roadblocks and bounces back quickly when problems arise. Effective communication skills (written or spoken) that are clear, concise and honest. Comfortable and excited to speak about the campaign publicly. Coach and learning mentality: successful experience or willingness to learn new things and pick up new skills on the job. Able to learn from mistakes and try again. Understanding of how your words and actions affect others, including an awareness of power language and communication accessibility. Ability to work weekends and weekday evenings, occasional holidays. Nice-to-Haves, but Not Required: Organizing experience in or around Grand Island, North Platte, Scottsbluff, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk Nebraska. Experience working for nonprofits and issue campaigns. Data Management and Evaluation Experience: Experience working with various data management systems and tools, mainly Google Suite. Experience with Relevant Campaign Tools and Technologies: VAN, Action Network, ThruText, MailChimp, eCRMs like EveryAction, or social media tools (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram). Event or Project Planning & Management, Implementation or Evaluation. Knowledge or previous experience working in roles that support constituents around affordability and action opportunities is a plus If you were here right now, you would be: Recruiting, training and developing activist leaders in your community to collect supporter petitions, educate others on key campaign issues, and recruit constituents to in-district events and actions. Planning and executing events for constituents around affordability as well as action opportunities including, but not limited to: door knocking, phonebanking, petitioning, visibility events, educational events, and more. Developing relationships with community leaders on corporate accountability, health care, and justice Engaging and expanding our support network through public visibility actions, voter outreach, and relationship-building. Salary, Benefits and Perks: The salary for this position is $55,000 to $67,000 for full-time. We offer a generous benefits package, including paid vacation and sick leave, health insurance, and hands-on training. At the end of the campaign, there may be opportunities for advancement and bonuses. At The Outreach Team, we prioritize equity and inclusion. We are an equal opportunity employer and we strongly encourage Black, indigenous, people of color, women, people with previous felony convictions, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and others who identify with underrepresented groups to apply. To Apply: Visit: https://theoutreachteam.applytojob.com/apply

item.title: Legislative Liaison
item.description: The Christian Business Partnership’s Legislative Liaison works for the Executive Director of The Partnership in serving as Christian business owners’ lead voice at the Ohio Statehouse and with lawmakers. His or her mission is to vigorously champion the religious freedom of Christian business owners while fostering a robust and open marketplace where innovation and competition allow every entrepreneur to succeed. Professional, personable, highly-organized, and deeply passionate about the Gospel and The Partnership’s mission, the Legislative Liaison plays an essential role in serving Christian business owners in Ohio. Reports to : Christian Business Partnership Executive Director Hours : Monday–Friday, 8:00am to 4:30pm Compensation : Full-time, Salaried/Exempt Location : CCV Office in Columbus, Ohio, with Occasional Statewide Travel Benefits : PTO (Paid Time Off), 10 Paid Holidays, Monthly Cell Phone Allotment, Mileage, Health, Vision, and Dental Insurance (CCV covers 75% of premium), Life Insurance, 4% Match on Retirement Plan Available after 1 Year Key Responsibilities Lead The Partnership’s efforts to advance legislative priorities at the Ohio Statehouse. Prepare and give legislative testimony in support of bills on The Partnership’s legislative agenda or in opposition to bills that undermine our mission. Stay “in-the-know” about issues facing Ohio’s communities, and especially Christianowned businesses. Conduct legislative research including reviewing legislation & amendments introduced in the General Assembly for impact on The Partnership’s issues. Draft Fact Sheets on The Partnership’s primary bills. Present The Partnership’s mission and information on issues at public speaking engagements and with the media. Provide periodic analysis and reports for management. Other duties as assigned. Job Qualifications & Requirements Skills and Experience Undergraduate degree required. 3-5 years of experience in policy-related field and knowledge of Ohio legislative process preferred. Strong research skills as well as proven verbal and written communication skills. Attentive to detail and well organized. Strong time management skills, punctual, able to operate on a schedule, meet deadlines, and manage multiple projects simultaneously. Flexible to accommodate shifting priorities. Ability to thrive in a multi-tasking, fast-paced work environment. Self-motivated daily by a passion to see The Partnership's work advance . Able to be proactive and strive to close gaps in skill and knowledge. Proficient in Google, Microsoft programs, and CRM database. Character and Spiritual Mature Christian, currently attending or pursuing attendance in a local church. Agreement with and adherence to CCV’s Statement of Faith and Code of Conduct. Demonstrated commitment to CCV’s mission and position on Core Issues. Ability to work discreetly with confidential information. Trustworthy, responsible, tactful, diplomatic, and focused on building consensus rather than emphasizing differences. Maintain a high level of professionalism focused on client/constituent relationships.

item.title: Senior Director Government Affairs
item.description: Description Oracle Corporate Affairs is seeking a Senior Director, Government Affairs . The Senior Director will report to the Senior Vice President, Government Affairs . In collaboration with a diverse portfolio of internal and external stakeholders, the Senior Director will serve as one of the company’s Legislative and Executive Branch lobbyists and a key advisor to senior company leaders. Working in close partnership with his / her government affairs colleagues, specific business units, and other relevant functional experts within the company, the candidate will identify, prioritize and lead advocacy efforts to drive domestic legislative, policy, and business initiatives. The ideal candidate understands the importance of the role to the success of the organization; has a robust understanding of information technology across a broad spectrum of business and policy priorities; has demonstrated success in achieving results in support of specific initiatives and objectives; and is experienced in working with the Democratic party. The Senior Director will be based in Washington, DC, and will be expected to primarily perform their duties as an in-office employee. Career Level - IC 5 Responsibilities QUALIFICATIONS DESIRED SKILLS Understanding of information technology policies. Experience in political giving strategies and working with corporate political action committees. Detail oriented, organized, and driven to follow-through and complete tasks. Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment, including experience with conceptualizing and leading projects independently with minimal supervision. Commitment to acting at all times with the highest integrity, including strict adherence to applicable laws and company values, which go beyond legal compliance. Qualifications Disclaimer: Certain U.S. based or U.S. customer or client-facing roles may be required to comply with applicable requirements, such as immunization/occupational health mandates, and/or drug testing requirements. Range and benefit information provided in this posting are specific to the stated locations only US: Hiring Range in USD from: $114,600 to $234,600 per annum. May be eligible for bonus, equity, and compensation deferral. Oracle maintains broad salary ranges for its roles in order to account for variations in knowledge, skills, experience, market conditions and locations, as well as reflect Oracle's differing products, industries and lines of business. Candidates are typically placed into the range based on the preceding factors as well as internal peer equity. Oracle US offers a comprehensive benefits package which includes the following: 1. Medical, dental, and vision insurance, including expert medical opinion 2. Short term disability and long term disability 3. Life insurance and AD&D 4. Supplemental life insurance (Employee/Spouse/Child) 5. Health care and dependent care Flexible Spending Accounts 6. Pre-tax commuter and parking benefits 7. 401(k) Savings and Investment Plan with company match 8. Paid time off: Flexible Vacation is provided to all eligible employees assigned to a salaried (non-overtime eligible) position. Accrued Vacation is provided to all other employees eligible for vacation benefits. For employees working at least 35 hours per week, the vacation accrual rate is 13 days annually for the first three years of employment and 18 days annually for subsequent years of employment. Vacation accrual is prorated for employees working between 20 and 34 hours per week. Employees working fewer than 20 hours per week are not eligible for vacation. 9. 11 paid holidays 10. Paid sick leave: 72 hours of paid sick leave upon date of hire. Refreshes each calendar year. Unused balance will carry over each year up to a maximum cap of 112 hours. 11. Paid parental leave 12. Adoption assistance 13. Employee Stock Purchase Plan 14. Financial planning and group legal 15. Voluntary benefits including auto, homeowner and pet insurance The role will generally accept applications for at least three calendar days from the posting date or as long as the job remains posted. Career Level - IC5

item.title: Legislative Representative
item.description: Legislative Representative City of New York Washington, New York, United States Full-time 1 day ago The Agency You’ll Join: The New York City Mayor’s Office is responsible for overseeing city services throughout the five boroughs, coordinating public agencies and departments, and managing public property. The administration is leading the fight in making the city more affordable, reducing inequality, improving public safety, ensuring delivery of efficient and effective services, and working to make New York City’s economy stronger. We value leadership, transparency, fairness, and efficiency as we actively seek diverse talents from various sectors to join our team. For current job opportunities, visit our careers page. The Team You’ll Work With: **NOTE: THIS ROLE IS LOCATED IN WASHINGTON, DC.** The Office of Federal Affairs coordinates the City's interaction with the Federal administration and Congress. The office keeps the Mayor and City agencies informed about pending or important issues affecting the City. The office also advocates on behalf of the city and is the DC liaison between the City and other cities seeking to work together on federal issues. The Problems You’ll Solve: The Legislative Representative will keep the Mayor and City agencies informed about pending or important issues affecting the City. About You: - You must have detailed knowledge of the Federal legislative process and elected officials. - You can demonstrate the understanding of and experience with any combination of the following: the City legislative process, public policy analysis, New York City and State agency operations, and lobbying. Minimum Required Qualifications: - Bachelor’s Degree. - 2+ years of relevant experience in New York City and State agency ecosystem, legislative, and operations processes. RESEARCH PROJECTS COOR(MA)-MGR - 0527A 1. Do you have a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university? 2. Do you have an associate degree from an accredited college or university along with two (2) years of experience with administrative, analytic, coordinative, supervisory or liaison responsibilities? 3. Do you have a four-year high school diploma, or its educational equivalent approved by a state's Department of Education or a recognized accrediting organization along with four (4) years of experience as described in question "2" above? 4. Do you have a satisfactory combination of education and/or experience equivalent to that described in questions "1," "2," and/or "3" above? The City of New York is an inclusive equal opportunity employer committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse workforce and providing a work environment that is free from discrimination and harassment based upon any legally protected status or protected characteristic, including but not limited to an individual's sex, race, color, ethnicity, national origin, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, gender identity, or pregnancy. Washington, New York, United States

item.title: Community Legislative Liaison Bureau Of Government Affairs
item.description: The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (The Health Department) protects and promotes the health of eight million New Yorkers with a budget of $2 billion, and roughly 7,000 staff. Central to this effort are programs that combat communicable diseases, expand access to health care, provide maternal health support, surveil human health conditions from chronic disease to mental health and substance use issues, and tackle other public health challenges. Pursuing effective public health policy is also vital to this work. The Legislative Affairs unit within the Bureau of Government Affairs plays a central role in DOHMH's ability to fulfil its mission by developing the agency's legislative agenda at the City, State and Federal levels, serving as the agency's point of contact for elected officials and coordinating legislative discussions with the Mayor's office and other City agencies. The Bureau also coordinates the Department's appearance at public hearings; maintain relationships with advocacy groups, civic organizations and lobbyists; and coordinates with the agency's press office and communications teams on external communications and events. The Community Affairs Unit helps the Department maintain good relations with elected officials, community boards, civic organizations, and other stakeholders by responding quickly and accurately to requests for information, organizing speakers for community events, problem solving and informing members of Department initiatives. The Legislative Affairs and Community Affairs units in the Office of External Affairs within the Bureau of Government Affairs seek to hire a Community Legislative Liaison. DUTIES WILL INCLUDE BUT NOT BE LIMITED TO: - Respond in a timely, concise, and intelligible fashion to inquiries from local elected officials, community boards and the general public - Attend and represent the Department at community board meetings, town halls, public meetings in response to day-to-day operations and public health emergencies - Disseminate public health information to community stakeholders and the public - Provides staffing and supporting role to the Public Information Office (PIO) during public health emergency activations - Participates in public health emergency trainings - Coordinate logistics of convening community/public forums and meetings with other city agencies and stake holders (e.g. hospitals) - Research, track, and analyze legislation and coordinate the department’s response in areas that may include the Office of Emergency Preparedness, Center for Population Health Data Science federal affairs, and other program areas as needed. - Prep executive-level leadership in the agency for public hearings and meetings with elected officials. - Cultivate and maintain relationships with other organizational units within the Health Department and other key partners. - Assist in developing and implementing legislative strategies. - Serve as a liaison to the Mayor’s Office by representing the Department’s position on public health issues and coordinating with internal partners. - Investigate and respond to elected official requests regarding general information on Health Department programs or actions. - Develop briefing materials and other content with research data and reports for the city council, state legislature, and federal government. - Maintenance of other internal unit and/or division organizational systems. - Respond in a timely, concise, and intelligible fashion to inquiries from local elected officials, community boards, and the general public - Special projects as assigned by the director PREFERRED SKILLS: - Excellent analytical, political, and writing skills. - Experience working in government and/or intergovernmental/legislative affairs. - Academic background in political science, public policy, public health, or related field. - Spreadsheets, Airtable, and data-tracking skills. - Must be self-motivated, able to work on multiple responsibilities simultaneously, and share the agency’s commitment to public health. Why you should work for us: - Loan Forgiveness: As a prospective employee of the City of New York, you may be eligible for federal/state loan forgiveness and repayment assistance programs that lessen your payments or even fully forgive your full balance. For more information, please visit the U.S. Department of Education’s website (https://studentaid.gov/pslf/) - Benefits: City employees are entitled to unmatched benefits such as: o a premium-free health insurance plan that saves employees over $10K annually, per a 2024 assessment. o additional health, fitness, and financial benefits may be available based on the position’s associated union/benefit fund. o a public sector defined benefit pension plan with steady monthly payments in retirement. o a tax-deferred savings program and o a robust Worksite Wellness Program that offers resources and opportunities to keep you healthy while serving New Yorkers. - Work From Home Policy: Depending on your position, you may be able to work up to two days during the week from home. - Job Security - you could enjoy more job security compared to private sector employment and be able to contribute to making NYC a healthy place to live and work. Established in 1805, the New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (NYC Health Department) is the oldest and largest health department in the U.S., dedicated to protecting and improving the health of NYC. Our mission is to safeguard the health of every resident and cultivate a city where everyone, regardless of age, background, or location, can achieve their optimal health. We provide a wide array of programs and services focused on food and nutrition, anti-tobacco support, chronic disease prevention, HIV/AIDS treatment, family and child health, environmental health, mental health, and social justice initiatives. As the primary population health strategist and policy authority for NYC, with a rich history of public health initiatives and scientific advancements, from addressing the 1822 yellow fever outbreak to the COVID-19 pandemic, we serve as a global leader in public health innovation and expertise. Come join us and help to continue our efforts in making a difference in the lives of all New Yorkers! item.title: Senior Administrative Assistant Government Affairs
item.description: Job Description General Summary: The Senior Administrative Assistant will serve as a trusted administrative partner to the Vice President, U.S. Government Affairs & Patient Advocacy; the Vice President, Federal Government Affairs; and the Executive Director, State Government Affairs. The role is responsible for complex calendar and travel management, meeting and event coordination, contracting and invoice administration, executive preparedness, and broader team operations. The successful candidate will work with a high degree of independence, judgment, discretion, and attention to detail while managing competing priorities and interacting professionally with senior internal and external stakeholders. Key Duties and Responsibilities: Executive and Stakeholder Support Serve as a primary administrative point of contact for supported leaders, anticipating needs, applying sound judgment, and appropriately screening, routing, prioritizing, and escalating requests. Build effective working relationships with senior executives, administrative colleagues, external consultants, government officials and their staff, trade associations, patient advocacy organizations, vendors, and other stakeholders. Handle confidential, sensitive, and time-critical information with discretion and professionalism. Complex Calendar Management Proactively manage complex and frequently changing calendars in Microsoft Outlook, including scheduling across multiple leaders, functions, sites, time zones, and external organizations. Resolve conflicts based on business priorities, protect time for critical work, and communicate scheduling tradeoffs and changes promptly. Ensure leaders have appropriate preparation time, meeting materials, locations, technology, and logistical information. Travel and Expense Administration Use Concur to independently arrange domestic and international travel, including air, ground transportation, lodging, itineraries, and other required logistics. Prepare and process accurate, timely expense reports and related correspondence; manage reimbursement inquiries and coordinate with travel agencies, airlines, hotels, and internal partners. Monitor and resolve time-sensitive travel and logistical issues during business travel, exercising judgment regarding when escalation is required. Contracting, Procurement, and Invoicing Coordinate the end-to-end administrative workflow for consultant and vendor agreements through Coupa and Icertis, including intake, routing, approvals, signatures, purchase orders, Statements of Work, invoicing, payment status, and record maintenance. Partner with Legal, Procurement, Finance, business owners, and external firms to support timely and compliant contracting and payment processes. Support vendor onboarding, invoice reconciliation, payment tracking, and basic departmental budget administration. Meetings, Conferences, and Events Plan and coordinate recurring team meetings, leadership meetings, conferences, off-sites, dinners, and external engagements. Manage venue sourcing, attendee communications, catering, transportation, audiovisual and technology needs, vendor coordination, on-site logistics, contracts, payments, and expense reconciliation, as applicable; integrate with Corporate Services as needed. Coordinate activities in accordance with company meeting, expense, procurement, and compliance requirements. Executive Preparedness and Document Support Develop agendas, gather and distribute pre-read materials, maintain organized reference files, and track administrative follow-ups and action items. Support the preparation, proofreading, formatting, and distribution of presentations, correspondence, reports, and other business documents. Help ensure supported leaders are prepared for meetings, travel, and external engagements while appropriately distinguishing administrative support from substantive government affairs content ownership. Team and Department Operations Support recurring business routines, team communications, shared calendars and resources, distribution and contact lists, onboarding and offboarding, office access, technology, facilities, and supply needs. Lead or support administrative and operational projects requiring coordination across functions, vendors, and external organizations. Collaborate with administrative colleagues across the organization, share administrative best practices, and provide or receive backup coverage as needed. Records, Compliance, and Process Management Maintain accurate and organized business records in accordance with company policies and applicable document-retention requirements. Follow established requirements for contracting, procurement, expenses, external engagements, and information handling; identify and escalate potential process or compliance issues appropriately. Use Microsoft 365 and other enterprise platforms to improve organization, communication, document management, and administrative efficiency Knowledge and Skills: Experience supporting multiple senior leaders, preferably at the Vice President level, in a complex and fast-paced organization. Experience in the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, healthcare, government affairs, public policy, or another highly regulated environment. Experience managing confidential matters and interacting with senior internal and external stakeholders. Experience with procurement, contracting, consultant or vendor administration, invoice workflows, and enterprise systems such as Concur, Coupa, and Icertis, or the ability to learn comparable platforms quickly. Advanced proficiency in Microsoft 365, including Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, with strong document-formatting, proofreading, and written communication skills. Demonstrated ability to effectively leverage AI-enabled productivity tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot and other approved enterprise technologies) to improve efficiency, enhance organization, streamline administrative processes, prepare meeting materials, conduct research, and support day-to-day business operations while exercising sound judgment and maintaining compliance with company policies. Proven ability to independently manage multiple projects and a high volume of daily work while maintaining accuracy, follow-through, and attention to detail. Strong judgment and problem-solving skills, including the ability to resolve non-routine issues, communicate conflicts and tradeoffs, and escalate matters appropriately. Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with a highly professional and service-oriented approach. Ability to anticipate needs, adapt quickly to changing priorities, and remain composed and effective under pressure. Excellent organizational skills, initiative, accountability, and motivation. Education and Experience: Typically requires high school or secondary school education Typically requires 2 years of administrative experience, or the equivalent combination of education and experience Pay Range: $39 - $58 Disclosure Statement: The range provided is based on what we believe is a reasonable estimate for the base salary pay range for this job at the time of posting. This role is eligible for an annual bonus and annual equity awards. Some roles may also be eligible for overtime pay, in accordance with federal and state requirements. Actual base salary pay will be based on a number of factors, including skills, competencies, experience, and other job-related factors permitted by law. At Vertex, our Total Rewards offerings also include inclusive market-leading benefits to meet our employees wherever they are in their career, financial, family and wellbeing journey while providing flexibility and resources to support their growth and aspirations. From medical, dental and vision benefits to generous paid time off (including a week-long company shutdown in the Summer and the Winter), educational assistance programs including student loan repayment, a generous commuting subsidy, matching charitable donations, 401(k) and so much more. Flex Designation: Hybrid-Eligible Or On-Site Eligible Flex Eligibility Status: In this Hybrid-Eligible role, you can choose to be designated as: 1. Hybrid : work remotely up to two days per week; or select 2. On-Site : work five days per week on-site with ad hoc flexibility. Note: The Flex status for this position is subject to Vertex’s Policy on Flex @ Vertex Program and may be changed at any time. #LI-Hybrid Company Information Vertex is a global biotechnology company that invests in scientific innovation. Vertex is committed to equal employment opportunity and non-discrimination for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to a person's race, color, sex, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital status, or any characteristic protected under applicable law. Vertex is an E-Verify Employer in the United States. Vertex will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities, in accordance with applicable law. Any applicant requiring an accommodation in connection with the hiring process and/or to perform the essential functions of the position for which the applicant has applied should make a request to the recruiter or hiring manager, or contact Talent Acquisition at ApplicationAssistance@vrtx.com

item.title: Legislative Auditor Tenncare
item.description: Legi slative Auditor: TennCare Location: Nashville, Tennessee Join us in our mission to make government work better. Role Snapshot The Legislative Auditor in the Division of Health Provider Review plays an important role in supporting accountability and transparency within TennCare, Tennessee’s Medicaid program. This position performs examinations and desk reviews of participating providers to ensure accuracy, compliance, and the appropriate use of state and federal resources. Why You'll Love This Job • Meaningful work that impacts communities across Tennessee • Flexible schedules and a standard 37.5-hour workweek • Opportunities for professional growth and development • Collaborative and supportive team environment • Comprehensive benefits and work-life balance What You'll Do • Conduct examinations and desk reviews of TennCare provider financial and statistical data to ensure accuracy and compliance. • Analyze cost reports, claims data, and supporting documentation for providers participating in the TennCare program. • Prepare clear, concise, and well-supported working papers that meet auditing standards and best practices. • Assist with development of tools to organize, track, and analyze information. • Perform data analysis to identify trends, inconsistencies, and issues that support audit conclusions and findings. • Communicate results and relevant information clearly to internal leadership, TennCare, and other stakeholders. • Collaborate with team members and support special projects such as rate computation and analysis, provider cost settlements, and reviews of Managed Care Contractors. What We’re Looking For Required: • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university with at least 24 semester hours in accounting • Ability to learn quickly, pay close attention to detail, think critically, problem solve, and produce high-quality work • Strong communication skills and ability to work independently and collaboratively • Good judgment and professionalism in interactions with auditees and coworkers Preferred: • Completed coursework or experience in data analytics • Progress toward or interest in obtaining the CPA license (30 semester hours in accounting), which is strongly encouraged for advancement Logistics • Travel: Seasonal travel may be required. Overnight stays are generally limited to Monday–Wednesday evenings based on auditee availability. • Compensation: Competitive salary and benefits, including annual and sick leave, insurance plans, pension, 401(k), college fee waivers, and flexible schedules. About the Office The Office of the Tennessee Comptroller of the Treasury audits state and local government entities and oversees financial and administrative management of state government. We are nationally recognized for professionalism and accountability and consistently rank as a Top Workplace. Learn more at www.comptroller.tn.gov Equal Opportunity Employer We are committed to fair and equal employment opportunities and maintaining a workplace free of discrimination and harassment. We prohibit discrimination based on race, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, religion, disability, veteran status, or any category protected by law. NOTICE This position requires a criminal background check. You may be required to provide information about your criminal history to be considered for this Texting TOS and Privacy Policy: Message type: informational; you will receive text messages regarding your application and potentially regarding interview scheduling. You can cancel the SMS service at any time. Just text "STOP" to the short code. item.title: Public Policy Associate
item.description: ABOUT PERPLEXITY Perplexity is AI for people who expect more. More accuracy. More agency. More signal, less noise. Our answer engine handles hundreds of millions of queries every month for people whose questions spark change and whose decisions bend the world toward progress. As our footprint grows, so does the number of policymakers, agencies, and civil society leaders who want to understand what we are building and how we think. ABOUT THE ROLE We're hiring a Public Policy Associate in Washington, D.C. to sit at the center of Perplexity's engagement with Congress, the executive branch, trade associations, think tanks, and the broader D.C. ecosystem. This work happens where Washington happens, in Hill offices, in coalition meetings across town, and at the occasional evening event where the conversations that matter most actually take place. This is a relationship heavy, execution heavy seat. You've already worked both sides of the table, once inside a congressional office and once representing an organization before Congress, and you know how policy actually moves. Our Comms team and executive leadership set the strategy; you're our boots on the ground who makes it real. You'll build the stakeholder map, carry our message into the rooms that matter, and bring back what policymakers are saying, so that Perplexity shows up early, credibly, and consistently on the policy questions shaping AI. WHAT YOU'LL DO Execute our policy communications strategy set by our Comms and executive leadership teams. Turn company positions into talking points, event backgrounders, and rapid response, and feed intelligence back to our legal, policy, and product teams. Build and hold relationships with Hill staff in personal offices and on committees, executive branch staff, trade associations, think tanks, and civil society organizations. Advocate directly. Take meetings, deliver our positions, and follow bills and rulemakings that affect Perplexity, working within the company's lobbying disclosure and ethics requirements. Run our D.C. event footprint. Hill staff briefings, roundtables, product demos, receptions, dinners, and off sites. Own guest lists, venues, run of show, and follow up. Represent Perplexity in coalitions and trade association working groups. Track what's being said, flag what matters, and bring our point of view into the conversation. Partner with think tanks and civil society groups on convenings, research launches, and joint programming. Prepare our leaders for D.C. engagements. Briefing books, meeting prep, and post meeting recaps that actually get read. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR At least 3 years of professional experience , including time on Capitol Hill in a personal office or on a committee is strongly preferred. External lobbying experience , either at a government relations or law firm representing clients, or in house at a company. Registered lobbying experience under the Lobbying Disclosure Act is strongly preferred. A real Washington network you built yourself, and the instinct to keep growing it. Event execution. You can run a 20 person Hill staff briefing or a 150 person reception end to end without anything slipping. Strong writing. You can turn a meeting into a two paragraph readout and a briefing book into something a principal will actually use. Sound judgment. You know what to escalate, what to handle, and how to represent a company in a room without a script. Genuine curiosity about AI policy and the substance of what Perplexity is building. You don't need to be a technologist, but you do need to want to learn. Comfort with the pace. Mornings, days, and evenings. This is a role for someone energized by the D.C. schedule. Based in Washington, D.C. and in office four days a week, with occasional travel. BONUS Hill experience on judiciary, commerce, intelligence, or AI focused portfolios. Experience staffing a principal at a company, agency, or trade association. Existing relationships across the AI and tech policy community in D.C.

item.title: Vice President Government Affairs
item.description: Over the last 20 years, Ares’ success has been driven by our people and our culture. Today, our team is guided by our core values – Collaborative, Responsible, Entrepreneurial, Self-Aware, Trustworthy – and our purpose to be a catalyst for shared prosperity and a better future. Through our recruitment, career development and employee-focused programming, we are committed to fostering a welcoming and inclusive work environment where high-performance talent of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives can build careers within this exciting and growing industry. Job Description Ares Management Corporation is looking to hire a Vice President to join its Government Affairs team. The position will be an exciting opportunity for an enthusiastic self-starter to help build and maintain Ares’ Government Affairs function. The Government Affairs function plays a crucial role in advancing the mission and objectives of Ares and our investors by engaging with policymakers across the globe, staying ahead of and responding to legislative and regulatory developments, and driving thought leadership and advocacy. The Vice President of Government Affairs will play a crucial role in building out the Government Affairs function. In this role, the ideal candidate will be responsible for executing on our policy agenda through monitoring policy developments, developing Ares viewpoints, and engaging in advocacy on behalf of the firm. We are looking for a self-directed individual who is a strong written and verbal communicator, is excited to partner with others and can work cross-functionally to execute on aligned priorities. Reporting relationships Reports to: Managing Director, Head of Government Affairs Primary functions and essential responsibilities Specific responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Partner with the Head of Government Affairs in executing the Government Affairs function strategy Monitor and assess impact of policy developments relevant to Ares and the alternative investment management industry Anticipate and assess opportunity, change, and potential risks in the legislative, regulatory, and political realms Shape legislative, regulatory, and administrative policies affecting the alternative investment industry Coordinate, participate in and manage Ares’ membership with trade groups Prepare briefing and presentation materials for engagements with policymakers, regulators, investors and other stakeholders Provide technical recommendations on legislative and regulatory proposals, collaborating closely with other teams to ensure alignment of views across the firm Represent Ares at meetings with government officials or staff, related events, and other relevant forums Collaborate closely with the Communications and Public Investor Relations teams, as well as other internal teams to ensure alignment between government affairs strategies, external communication and Ares’ overall objectives Provide oversight and direction for external government affairs resources, where appropriate From time to time, assist with portfolio company matters involving government stakeholders Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s Degree is required MPA, MPP, MBA, JD, CFA preferred Experience and Skills Required: 8-12 years of relevant experience working in or with legislative, regulatory, or executive branch agencies Prior experience in government affairs for financial services Prior experience writing and contributing to comment letters, drafting legislative language, and developing policy viewpoints for financial services Detailed understanding of and relationships with financial services policymakers Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint and Word General Requirements: Extensive policy, advocacy, and analytical expertise Superior written and verbal communication skills and a demonstrated ability to create content for specified audiences Demonstrated ability to drive consensus among a diverse array of interests and priorities Exceptional client service orientation and ability to collaborate cross functionally Outstanding organizational skills with strong attention to detail Strong time management and prioritization skills Good judgment in terms of escalating issues vs. solving problems independently Comfort in dealing with ambiguity and uncertainty in a dynamic and fast-paced environment Proven ability to learn quickly, display flexibility and adaptability Political awareness, discretion and demonstrated ability to manage sensitive and high impact matters Highest degree of integrity and ethics Reporting Relationships Compensation The anticipated base salary range for this position is listed below. Total compensation may also include a discretionary performance-based bonus. Note, the range takes into account a broad spectrum of qualifications, including, but not limited to, years of relevant work experience, education, and other relevant qualifications specific to the role. $185,000-$250,000 The firm also offers robust Benefits offerings. Ares U.S. Core Benefits include Comprehensive Medical/Rx, Dental and Vision plans; 401(k) program with company match; Flexible Savings Accounts (FSA); Healthcare Savings Accounts (HSA) with company contribution; Basic and Voluntary Life Insurance; Long-Term Disability (LTD) and Short-Term Disability (STD) insurance; Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and Commuter Benefits plan for parking and transit. Ares offers a number of additional benefits including access to a world-class medical advisory team, a mental health app that includes coaching, therapy and psychiatry, a mindfulness and wellbeing app, financial wellness benefit that includes access to a financial advisor, new parent leave, reproductive and adoption assistance, emergency backup care, matching gift program, education sponsorship program, and much more. There is no set deadline to apply for this job opportunity. Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the search is no longer active.

item.title: Director Government Affairs
item.description: As a leader in advancing New York’s energy transition, the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA) is a credible, objective and trusted partner in energy planning and in deploying new innovative technologies to build an affordable, abundant, reliable, and clean energy system. NYSERDA works with stakeholders statewide, including residents, business owners, developers, community leaders, local government officials, universities, utilities, investors, entrepreneurs, and more, to develop, invest, and foster conditions that: Attract the private sector capital investment needed to expand New York’s clean energy economy. Advance solutions for using clean energy at a large-scale in New York. Enable New York’s communities and residents to benefit equitably in the clean energy transition. Job Overview The Director, Government Affairs reports directly to the VP for Policy Implementation & Intergovernmental Affairs. The Director oversees a Government Affairs (GA) team charged with interfacing with the Executive Chamber, the State Legislature, municipal officials, other state and local agencies and authorities and other key stakeholders to advance NYSERDA’s Mission Outcomes. This work includes crafting and stewarding a proactive strategy to advance Authority priorities, responding to incoming requests from these entities, informing energy and environmental policy discussions that pertain to NYSERDA, developing responses to enacted legislation, and other engagements as needed. Primary Responsibilities Lead NYSERDA engagement with local and state elected officials and staff, including leading development and management of engagement with Legislature and Executive Chamber, support NYSERDA Officers, particularly the CEO, at events, and preparation of background and briefing materials for Senior Executives. Coordinate with Vice President, Policy Implementation & Intergovernmental Affairs and Chief of Staff’s office to develop approach to annual Budget/Legislative Session, including preparation for the President and CEO and Officers at legislative hearings and committee meetings, and ongoing engagement with Chamber and Legislative branches. . In close coordination with NYSERDA Officers and Counsel’s office, manage Legislative Departmental submissions and responses to all legislative inquiries, as well as inform NYSERDA management of legislative developments throughout the State Legislature Session. Prepare and conduct briefings for Executive Team, Officers, and CEO on changes to or opportunities to obtain new critical funding or regulatory actions occurring at federal, state and local levels that would impact the Authority’s ability to advance its responsibilities. Manage and oversee all relations with local and state elected officials and their staff. Oversee constituent services and responses. Coordinate with Communications Team, Events Team, Executive Team and program departments to handle and respond to events, press, etc. Attend and represent NYSERDA at events as needed, including speaking at events, conferences, and functions, as needed. Provide excellent verbal and written products, including ability to craft a compelling business/strategic case for Authority outcomes. Write and edit internal and external communications. Serve as an effective coach and leader providing relevant strategic and management guidance to members of the GA Team as well as other departments. Maintain a robust knowledge of local, state, and Federal key issues, priorities, agenda, and sensitivities, particularly as it relates to climate, clean energy, and electrification. Perform all managerial and supervisory responsibilities with respect, fairness, consistency, and inclusion across the workforce. Other duties assigned to support the Authority’s mission and outcomes. Minimum Qualifications A Bachelor’s degree and 10 years of legislative or relevant experience, including 5 years in supervisory roles In depth knowledge and understanding of legislative processes and actions In-depth understanding of New York State Government and agencies. Genuine passion for advancing sound policy relating to energy and the environment and an interest in developing and supporting a dynamic and talented team. Project management and leadership skills including the ability to work as a team leader and team member, maintain project timelines, budgets, and deliver on commitments. Highest level of communication and interpersonal skills involving the ability to work cross-functionally to understand requirements, present alternatives and recommendations. Self-starter who acts independently, directs one’s own work and can handle diverse tasks quickly and accurately within a high-performance environment. Exceptional manager, coach, mentor, and developer of talent; an ability to lead and develop a team to achieve their potential, innovate and uncover new possibilities, and deliver impactful and relevant outcomes. Demonstrated problem-solving ability, resourcefulness, adaptability, and an instinct for surfacing value and pragmatic solutions. Top-notch presentation and interpersonal skills that resonate with audiences of diverse backgrounds. Relentless work ethic and resolute integrity Strong organizational and analytical skills; ability to quickly aggregate and analyze information. Willingness to occasionally work long or odd hours, especially during Legislative session. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree and 8 years’ experience in legislative and government affairs position including 5 years in supervisory roles. Specific experience in energy or environmental policy. Please submit your resume. Cover letters are welcome but not required. To receive full consideration please apply by 09/14/2026. Please note that during the application process, you may be prompted to opt-in to Artificial Intelligence (“AI”) scoring. This is an automatic request in the ADP system but is not a feature that is used by NYSERDA in its recruiting and hiring process. Your response will have no impact on your application to NYSERDA. For further information on our hiring policies, employment opportunities for people with disabilities and EEO please click on this link and scroll down to the Policies section. [INDGER]

item.title: Political Reporter
item.description: Reporter – New Orleans politics The Times-Picayune has an opening for one of the best beats around: covering the public officials, civic leaders and other bastions of political power in New Orleans. Politics in the Crescent City are dagger sharp and always interesting. We’re looking for an experienced reporter who can navigate the city’s centers of power and the personalities who control them. The goal is to tell great stories about how politics – and the fight for political power – impact the everyday lives of New Orleanians. The city’s passionate politics are an outgrowth of its unique culture, neighborhoods and people. It also has a locally owned, Pulitzer-Prize winning media company that’s served readers for nearly two centuries. The Times-Picayune and our website, NOLA.com, offer distinctive, impactful journalism every day, produced by a team of journalists with decades of experience covering south Louisiana. The company is an equal opportunity employer, committed to recruiting, developing, and promoting a diverse workforce while providing unique opportunities and career paths for our employees. We encourage applicants of all backgrounds and experience levels to apply. This position offers a competitive salary and benefits package that includes medical, vision and dental insurance, short term disability, long term disability and a 401K plan.

item.description: Our team members are at the heart of everything we do. At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today! We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented apprentice to join our U.S. Public Policy & Advocacy team. This co-op offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in public policy, advocacy, and legislative affairs. The co-op will support various facets of our team's needs, including policy analysis, administrative tasks, and project support—right next to the U.S. House of Representatives’ House Office Buildings. This hybrid role includes in-person opportunities in our office and on Capitol Hill. Location: Washington, DC Hours: Full-time Duration: 6 months Primary Duties and Responsibilities: Support Specialist Role with Administrative Duties (non-email and calendar related): Prepare presentations and create slide decks for team presentations (Specialist, U.S. Public Policy, U.S. Federal Advocacy). Develop "footprint" one-pagers for advocacy efforts (U.S. Federal Advocacy). Facilities List: Exported Data Project (Specialist, U.S. Federal Advocacy): Review and verify asset types (e.g., ensure facilities are correctly categorized such as offices vs. warehouses). Assist the Specialist with communications and organization involving internal teams working to update facility data. Collaborate with IT to create a formalized data export system, potentially developing a website similar to DCC and GNP platforms (Specialist, U.S. Federal Advocacy, Real Estate, Customer Data, IT). Attend Hearings and Industry Briefings: Take notes and draft memos summarizing key takeaways for the team (Full Team). Participate in and take notes for state advocacy coalition calls (State Team). Assist the State Team in facilitating and documenting regular state consultant calls. Federal Policy Support: Assist the Federal Policy team with risk register input. Track and analyze key public policy developments, including executive orders, regulations, legislative proposals, and more. Support for Meetings, Lobbying, and PAC Operations: Input and organize data related to meeting/lobbying/PAC conversations using tracking software or processes (U.S. Federal Advocacy Education Requirements: Currently enrolled in a graduate school with an upcoming completion of a master's degree. Must be able to work 40 hours per week. Minimum Skills, Knowledge and Responsibilities: Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing Good project management skills Strong interpersonal, teamwork, and leadership skills Good analytical, conceptual and problem solving skills to evaluate business problems and apply knowledge to identify appropriate solutions Must be eager to learn, self-motivated, flexible, accountable and can effectively handle multiple tasks at one time Excellent organizational and time-management skills Knowledge of computers to operative effectively with PowerPoint presentations, Excel spreadsheets, and Microsoft Outlook What Cencora offers We provide compensation, benefits, and resources that enable a highly inclusive culture and support our team members’ ability to live with purpose every day. In addition to traditional offerings like medical, dental, and vision care, we also provide a comprehensive suite of benefits that focus on the physical, emotional, financial, and social aspects of wellness. This encompasses support for working families, which may include backup dependent care, adoption assistance, infertility coverage, family building support, behavioral health solutions, paid parental leave, and paid caregiver leave. To encourage your personal growth, we also offer a variety of training programs, professional development resources, and opportunities to participate in mentorship programs, employee resource groups, volunteer activities, and much more. For details, visit https://www.virtualfairhub.com/cencora Full time $29,600 - 54,340 *This Salary Range reflects a National Average for this job. The actual range may vary based on your locale. Ranges in Colorado/California/Washington/New York/Hawaii/Vermont/Minnesota/Massachusetts/Illinois State-specific locations may be up to 10% lower than the minimum salary range, and 12% higher than the maximum salary range. Equal Employment Opportunity Cencora is committed to providing equal employment opportunity without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, national origin, age, disability, veteran status or membership in any other class protected by federal, state or local law. item.title: Public Policy Manager
item.description: JOB SUMMARY: The Manager of Public Policy is a member of Truth Initiative's Public Policy team and advances the organization's policy priorities by conducting strategic policy research and analysis; monitoring and evaluating legislative, regulatory, and public health developments related to nicotine and substance use, cannabis, opioids, and other emerging public health issues; developing policy reports, issue briefs; and supporting policy advocacy efforts through research, coalition engagement, and stakeholder education. In addition to contributing to work on nicotine and tobacco issues, The Manager serves as a subject matter expert on substance use and addiction policy issues and works collaboratively across Truth Initiative to translate complex policy developments into actionable insights, evidence-based recommendations, and audience-appropriate materials. DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES (*ESSENTIAL DUTIES): Monitor, research, and analyze federal, state, and local legislation, regulations, and policy developments related to nicotine and tobacco, substance use prevention, cannabis regulation, opioid misuse and overdose prevention, addiction treatment, and related public health issues.* Identify policy trends, emerging issues, and opportunities for organizational engagement, public education, and policy impact.* Produce policy analyses, issue briefs, fact sheets, regulatory summaries, white papers, reports, and other written products.* Draft and support the development of formal comments to federal and state agencies.* Synthesize scientific literature, policy research, surveillance data, and public health evidence into actionable policy recommendations.* Attend and report on hearings, regulatory meetings, policy briefings, and conferences.* Build and maintain relationships with external partners, coalitions, public health organizations, academic institutions, and governmental agencies. Represent Truth Initiative in external meetings, working groups, coalitions, and professional conferences. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: Master's degree in Public Policy, Public Health, Health Policy, Political Science, Law, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience. 5-7 years of professional experience in public policy, government affairs, health policy, public health advocacy, regulatory affairs, or policy research and analysis. Demonstrated experience in substance use prevention policy, opioid policy, cannabis policy, addiction treatment policy, behavioral health policy, and tobacco control policy. Preferred candidate would have previous exposure to substance use prevention world and contacts Experience monitoring and analyzing legislative and regulatory activity at the federal and/or state levels. Excellent public health policy research and analytical skills. Strong writing, editing, and policy communication skills. Ability to interpret legislation, regulations, scientific evidence, and public health data. Strong project management and organizational skills. Ability to build productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders. PREFFERED QUALIFICATIONS: Experience working on federal public health, substance use, healthcare, behavioral health, or regulatory policy issues. Familiarity with federal legislative and regulatory processes and agencies including FDA, CDC, SAMHSA, NIH, CMS, DEA, ONDCP, and HHS. Experience drafting or contributing to public comments, Congressional briefings, policy recommendations, or regulatory analyses. Experience engaging with federal agencies, Congressional offices, national advocacy organizations, or public health coalitions. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This position is based in Washington, D.C. with a hybrid work schedule of three days in the office and two telework days. COMPENSATION PACKAGE: The salary range for this role is starting at $85,000-$90,000 per year on a national basis. Individual pay decisions are based on a number of factors, including but not limited to qualifications for the role, relevant work experience, skillset, internal equity, location, and certifications, consistent with applicable law. Salary is just one part of our total rewards package which additionally includes performance bonus for eligible roles, and competitive benefits. Interested candidates should submit their cover letter and resume here OR mail application materials to: Human Resources Attn: Public Policy Manager 900 G Street, NW Fourth Floor Washington, DC 20001 Fax: (202) 204-5214 No telephone calls please. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status or disability.

item.title: Government Affairs Specialist
item.description: The Government Affairs Specialist supports the company's government and regulatory affairs efforts by monitoring and tracking legislative, regulatory, and public policy developments at the international, federal, state, and local levels. Reporting to the Manager of Government Relations, this role coordinates policy updates, prepares monthly reporting materials, supports industry association engagement, and assists in identifying emerging compliance matters, including data privacy regulations. Responsibilities: Monitor and track international legislative and regulatory developments that may impact the business. Assist the Government and Regulatory Affairs team with U.S. legislative, regulatory, and government affairs activities at the federal, state, and local levels. Research, identify, and track regulatory actions and emerging public policy issues. Prepare and distribute monthly government relations updates and reporting materials. Support participation in industry associations and serve as an alternate representative on select committees. Monitor developing data privacy laws and compliance requirements, including CPRA, GDPR, and similar regulations. Summarize policy developments and communicate potential business impacts to internal stakeholders. Collaborate with internal teams and external partners to support the company's government relations objectives. Job Requirements: Associate’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Public Administration, or related experience required. Proven experience in government relations, advocacy, public policy, legislative affairs, or a related field preferred. Understanding of federal, state, and local legislative and regulatory processes. Strong organizational, research, and analytical skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and collaborate effectively within a team environment. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, primarily Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Ability to influence others, maintain confidentiality, and exercise sound judgment. Must be able to work full-time onsite in Middleville, Michigan. This is not a remote position. Middleville, Michigan, United States

item.title: Director Of Government Affairs Office Of The Secretary Of War
item.description: RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: No relocation assistance available CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes CLEARANCE TYPE: Top Secret TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. The Director of Government Affairs will report directly to the Senior Director, Office of the Secretary of War Customer Relations Team within the Northrop Grumman Corporate Global Business Development organization. Located in Falls Church, VA, the selected candidate will be responsible for expanding and maintaining effective relations between Northrop Grumman and the Department of War, focused on organizations within the Office of the Secretary of War (including Policy, CAPE, and Comptroller) and the Joint Staff. The Director will directly engage with government officials to support Northrop Grumman policy objectives and facilitate engagements for company leaders. Specific responsibilities will include but not be limited to the following: Designing, coordinating, and executing customer engagement plans in support Northrop Grumman policy and program priorities. Providing insights into Department of War policy, personnel, programmatic, budgetary, and legislative initiatives affecting company equities. Orchestrating engagements with organizations within the Office of the Secretary of War with other elements of Northrop Grumman (e.g., Military Service teams) to maximize effectiveness. Effectively representing Northrop Grumman senior leadership views and positions with senior Department of War officials. Basic Qualifications Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of 10 years of combined experience in U.S. Government policy and/or defense industry business development or government affairs. Demonstrated experience working with the Department of War, including impactful relationships within the Office of the Secretary of War and Joint Staff. Proven ability to think strategically and integrate policy, political, requirement, and budgetary considerations to inform senior U.S. Government civilian and military decision makers. Knowledgeable of Department of War processes, including PPBE and Acquisition, and familiarity with ongoing policy reforms. Excellent organizational, verbal, and written communication skills, as well as project management, analytical, planning, and presentation skills. Active Top Secret security clearance with the ability to obtain the SCI; maintaining the required security clearance will be a condition of continued employment. Preferred Qualifications Master’s degree in National Security or related discipline and/or a minimum of 15 years of combined experience in U.S. Government policy and/or defense industry business development or government affairs Executive presence to include a high level of judgement, initiative, integrity, and hands-on approach to problem solving both internal and external to the company. A team player, self-starter, with a strong work ethic and ability to work cooperatively across the organization without significant support. Primary Level Salary Range: $203,900.00 - $305,900.00 The above salary range represents a general guideline; however, Northrop Grumman considers a number of factors when determining base salary offers such as the scope and responsibilities of the position and the candidate's experience, education, skills and current market conditions. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay. Annual bonuses are designed to reward individual contributions as well as allow employees to share in company results. Employees in Vice President or Director positions may be eligible for Long Term Incentives. In addition, Northrop Grumman provides a variety of benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, Company paid holidays and paid time off (PTO) for vacation and/or personal business. The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. Northrop Grumman is an Equal Opportunity Employer, making decisions without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected class. For our complete EEO and pay transparency statement, please visit http://www.northropgrumman.com/EEO. U.S. Citizenship is required for all positions with a government clearance and certain other restricted positions.
