item.title: Election Equipment Technician Ballot Processing Specialist
item.description: Election Equipment Technician (Ballot Processing Specialist) Abacus Chicago, Illinois, United States Contract 19 days ago Election Equipment Technician (Ballot Processing Specialist): (# 5-10 openings) – Services would start on or about 41 days before each Election Day and end on or about 21 days after each Election Day, seven (7) days a week. 1. Pre-LAT (Logic and Accuracy Testing) of electronic voting equipment. For Pre-LAT, basic computer skills are required and responsibilities include; a . Sealing and packing election equipment b. Recording seal numbers on the official Seal Accountability Form c. Field Technicians supporting approximately 17-40 precincts per assignment cycle 2. Load voter registration data into Electronic Poll Book (EPB) devices and test those devices; 3. Load election data on to touch-screen voting devices and test the unit to correct results; 4. 4. Load data and test ballot scanners to ensure correct results; 5. Test to make sure that all ballots from touchscreen voting device and preprinted ballots are run through ballot scanner device and are accurately transmitted successfully; 6. Change paper rolls on the Ballot scanners; 7. Resetting the touchscreen and Electronic Poll Book to Election Mode, and the Ballot Scanner to show a zero; 8. Packing equipment and making sure all items are included; 9. Setup and take down- duties will require lifting of up to 60 lbs. and include: a. Set up, open, plug in and turn on touchscreen voting devices, electronic poll book, printers and ballot scanners. b. Take down all units and transport them from the Pre- LAT area to the ESCs. c. Electronic Poll book, Ballot Scanner, Printer and TouchScreen final check. Duties require lifting of up to 60 lbs., extended walking and standing over an extended period of time. d. Check touchscreens and E-Poll book to insure they are in "election " mode, having the proper date and time, and checking the scanners for a zero (0) tape. e. Place touchscreen voting devices, E-Pollbook, printers and ballot scanners into ESC. Ballot Prep. Duties: Require light-to-moderate manual labor involving 20-30 lb. boxes of paper ballots, including unboxing, separating, shrink-wrapping, checking off and distributing to corresponding ESC Need Computer knowledge: This role may include some data-entry work. Personnel Conduct Requirements (For all the jobs – add this 4 jobs) 1. Workers are allowed to wear casual attire. Jeans, knee-length shorts, work boots and gym shoes are acceptable. Personnel assigned to work on the Dock or pushing ESC's are required to wear steel-toe boots . No political rhetoric or profanity on clothing, ripped jeans, open-toe shoes, or Crocs. 2. Smoking is permitted ONLY outside the facility located at 1819 West Temporary Staffing – Central Office Headquarters & Warehouse RFP Pershing Street and must occur at least 15 feet away from the entrance. 3. Workers are not allowed to have mobile devices on their person while on the production floor. This includes the use of headphones or Bluetooth devices, 4. Workers are not allowed to sleep in the Warehouse at any time. 5. Workers should only eat and drink in designated areas. Never on the production floor. 6. The manager and assistant manager will be providing employee schedules. By applying for this job, you agree to receive calls, AI-generated calls, text messages, or emails from and its affiliates, and contracted partners. Frequency varies for text messages. Message and data rates may apply. Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages. You can reply STOP to cancel and HELP for help. You can access our privacy policy at Privacy Policy - Abacus . Chicago, Illinois, United States

item.title: Congressional Affairs Analyst
item.description: About Chartis Federal Chartis Federal is a premier systems engineering and integration firm specializing in mission-critical IT and communications solutions for law enforcement, homeland security, and defense. As a trusted prime contractor with over $160 million in task order awards, we operate across 22 states and support essential government missions worldwide. Our commitment to excellence has fueled our year-over-year growth, earning us recognition twice as a Washington Technology FAST 50 company and securing a place on the Inc. 5000 list for five consecutive years. At Chartis Federal, our mission is clear: keeping heroes safe and connected—on the battlefield, on the border, and in our backyards. Position Overview We are seeking a Congressional Affairs Analyst to support the customer’s Secretary of the General Staff (SGS) with congressional correspondence, legislative tracking, and staff-action tasking. This role drafts responses to Congressional Requests for Information, tracks legislation and hearings, and ensures outgoing correspondence meets regulatory and formatting standards. The ideal candidate brings strong research and writing skills along with the ability to synthesize complex legislative and regulatory information for senior leadership review. This position is contingent upon contract award. Responsibilities · Enter and track taskers in the Electronic Tasking System (ETS) and Task Management Tool (TMT) received via the Correspondence and Management Tasking System (CATMS) and HQDA ETS; determine OPR, staffing requirements, and suspense dates. · Draft and recommend responses to Congressional Requests for Information (RFIs), Report Requirements, and letters from Members of Congress; distribute RFIs to the appropriate Directorate and set suspense dates for leadership review. · Support Congressional Hearings and leadership engagements by preparing draft and final materials for Director/Deputy Director, Army National Guard testimony and correspondence. · Track, compile, and summarize Congressional legislation, hearings, and audits (Army Audit Agency, DoD Inspector General, GAO) to inform senior leader decisions. · Review and edit outgoing correspondence for compliance with NGB, HQDA, and ARNG format, grammar, content, and regulatory standards. · Provide procedural guidance on staffing actions and facilitate weekly Workflow Manager synchronization meetings. · Consolidate and review weekly situation reports, task trackers, and key working initiatives for distribution to division Action Officers. · 5+ years of experience in congressional correspondence, legislative tracking, or staff-action/correspondence management in a DoD or federal environment. · Demonstrated research and writing skills, with the ability to produce accurate, well-formatted responses under deadline pressure. · Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience (preferred). · Congressional correspondence or legislative tracking experience a plus. · Familiarity with AR 25-50/ARNG Memorandum 25-52 correspondence standards a plus. · Must have active SECRET clearance. Why Join Chartis Federal? We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package, including: · Comprehensive health insurance (medical, dental, vision) · Retirement plans with company contributions · Professional development opportunities and career growth support · A dynamic and collaborative work environment where your contributions are valued At Chartis Federal, we believe in fostering a culture of excellence, integrity, and innovation while supporting critical national security missions. Join us in shaping the future of government contracting and national security solutions. Chartis Federal is an Equal Opportunity Employer and employs qualified individuals regardless of race, religion, color, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other classification proscribed under applicable law. We participate in E-Verify.

item.title: Senior Public Policy Analyst Medicaid Hybrid
item.description: Resp & Qualifications PURPOSE: The Senior Public Policy Analyst monitors, evaluates, and provides recommendations on strategy and communications regarding federal and state public policy issues in support of the companys business priorities. The Senior Analyst is responsible for policy development on key issues, ensuring the Public Policy and Government Affairs (PPGA) team effectively communicates federal and state policy proposals and their specific impacts to the rest of the organization, as well as identifying issues for potential advocacy external to CareFirst. The incumbent will have primary responsibility for issues related to Medicaid. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Serving as policy subject matter expert on key legislative and regulatory developments impacting Medicaid and Medicaid managed care organizations. Providing internal education and policy briefings on government action and policy trends to assist in business decisions across the company. Conducting legislative, regulatory, and policy research and analysis. Developing external communications, written materials, and thought leadership to communicate CareFirsts policy perspective and advance meaningful discussion on pressing health policy issues (e.g., talking points, fact sheets, public comments, blog posts, subject matter expert panels). Providing guidance on external messaging on CareFirst initiatives. Conducting internal policy development on key issues to position CareFirst as a thought leader. Monitoring and participating in legislative, regulatory, and stakeholder bodies and workgroups. Building relationships with business leadership by providing clear executive-level presentations, regular check-in meetings, and rapid response policy analysis. Representing CareFirst on work groups at our trade and other external organizations. Conducting research for use in drafting position papers, written and verbal testimony for presentation before legislative and regulatory bodies, correspondence, and other responses for public policy and governmental affairs purposes and research leading to the development of corporate positions. SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY: Position does not have direct reports but is expected to assist in guiding and mentoring less experienced staff. May lead a team of matrixed resources. Experience: 5 years experience in health care policy environment focused on policy and communication. In-depth understanding of healthcare payor industry and operational processes and impacts of regulatory guidance. Understanding of insurance products and regulatory environment. Proven analytical and problem-solving skills to evaluate business processes and recommend effective solutions. Experience in project management, business process analysis, workflow, and task analysis. Analytical skills and understanding of where to find information germane to mandates. Written and oral communications skills. Ability to work with all levels within the organization and to build highly cooperative and productive relationships. Ability to coordinate multiple public policy activities within a dynamic environment. Ability to communicate to diverse audiences through a variety of methods. Ability to work with senior management and with their full confidence. Ability to present complex ideas to create a clear picture of impacts to the organization. Ability to act on behalf of management in a manner that is consistent with divisional vision. Ability to act in consultative manner to project teams charged with operationalizing mandates. PC skills, including Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Must be able to meet established deadlines and handle multiple customer service demands from internal and external customers, within set expectations for service excellence. item.title: Manager Public Policy Southeast Gulf
item.description: Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way. The Community you will join: Airbnb’s Public Policy campaign team exists to further the interests of our community of hosts and guests with politicians, regulators, opinion leaders and others who shape the political and regulatory context for our business, helping them to understand the significant social and economic contributions of our platform. Across the North America (“NAMER”) region, US and Canada specifically, we are engaged in hundreds of local conversations and negotiations with governments big and small. We engage governments at local, state, provincial and national levels directly and also use innovative advocacy and partnership strategies that actively involve our community and stakeholders in making the case for fair, progressive home sharing rules. The Difference You Will Make: The main role of the Public Policy Manager is to ensure the conception and execution of successful policy campaigns in their assigned region. In coordination with the Public Policy Lead, the Public Policy Manager will draft, develop and execute integrated government relations, communications, stakeholder engagement and mobilization plans and projects to achieve key policy objectives As a Public Policy Manager, you must be meticulously organized, detail- and solutions-oriented. You are also able to see the big picture and prioritize projects strategically when needed, while understanding how to synthesize legislation, information and data that should be escalated to leadership. You should have a strong independent work ethic and excellent communication skills, and an ability to take big ideas and translate them into policy with a positive and creative outlook. The ability to develop and maintain good and strong relationships with key internal functions and stakeholders in the region and globally within Airbnb will be highly valued. A Typical Day: Develop and implement Airbnb’s legislative and public policy objectives; including helping determine advocacy priorities, positions, and strategies. Review legislative language, draft comments, and research issues to provide analysis and critical thinking on legislation affecting Airbnb’s priorities. Maintain relationships with an extensive network of contacts in local, regional, and national legislative, executive, and administrative offices, as well as with allied groups and coalition partners. Represent Airbnb in meetings with government and elected officials, as well as industry associations, Airbnb hosts, and other stakeholders. Represent Airbnb at public speaking engagements as directed by the Head of Public Policy. Manage consultants and agencies to support campaign plans. Ensure progress is reported accurately and regularly, and roadblocks flagged in a timely fashion. Works closely with cross functional partners to make sure that policy plans fit with business priorities. Monitor and track legislation and regulatory matters as directed. Support as needed to help implement Airbnb’s legislative and public policy activities. Your Expertise: 8+ years experience working with policy issues in a relevant business, political, governmental, legislative or regulatory context such as tourism and accommodation business, e-commerce / internet / platform regulation, housing and landlord/tenant law, or tax issues. Ability to quickly get up to speed on complex technical and regulatory issues. Ability to manage multiple complex projects simultaneously and navigate complex matrix organization with multiple stakeholders. Strong analytical and critical thinking skills; planning, memo-writing and budgeting/basic accounting skills with proficiency in major computer applications. Extremely creative; takes an entrepreneurial approach to the work with a proven track Record of being proactive. Highly results-driven and strives to find the most efficient way to do things without sacrificing a high quality of work and/or results. Excellent communicator with great presentation and writing skills Acute attention to detail; extremely organized and able to help keep others organized. Strong work ethic, and exhibits professionalism, courtesy and strong interpersonal skills. Ability to exercise judgment and maintain confidentiality. Flexible with the ability to remain poised under pressure; adapts to situations as they arise. Embraces change and challenges with a positive and solutions-oriented approach. Self-starter with a sense of humor and the ability to thrive in a fast moving and sometimes stressful environment; ability to resolve complex and unfamiliar problems in a timely and efficient manner. Passion for home-sharing and the mission of the company. Leadership skills and experience in managing other people and developing teams will be nice to have. Willingness to travel regularly within the assigned region. Your Location: Due to the nature of this position, the successful applicant will need to be based in New Orleans, LA or Atlanta, GA to be able to conduct their work. If your position is employed by another Airbnb entity, your recruiter will inform you what states you are eligible to work from. Our Commitment To Inclusion & Belonging: Airbnb is committed to working with the broadest talent pool possible. We believe diverse ideas foster innovation and engagement, and allow us to attract creatively-led people, and to develop the best products, services and solutions. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply. We strive to also provide a disability inclusive application and interview process. If you are a candidate with a disability and require reasonable accommodation in order to submit an application, please contact us at: reasonableaccommodations@airbnb.com . Please include your full name, the role you’re applying for and the accommodation necessary to assist you with the recruiting process. We ask that you only reach out to us if you are a candidate whose disability prevents you from being able to complete our online application.

item.description: Project Manager – RFP & Vendor Selection Leading PA IT Firm Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, United States Contract 9 days ago Hybrid Schedule: 3 days on-site Job Overview The Project Manager will lead the development and procurement process for a large-scale automated licensing system replacement, overseeing RFP development, vendor evaluation, contract negotiations, and award. This role will coordinate stakeholders, subject matter experts, legal teams, and vendors while ensuring the project complies with applicable procurement requirements, policies, procedures, and project management standards. Job Duties Develop, control, and maintain a comprehensive project management plan and schedule covering RFP development, vendor bid management, proposal evaluation, negotiations, and contract award. Lead the development of a comprehensive RFP documenting business, functional, technical, licensing, and enhancement requirements for a replacement automated licensing system. Ensure RFP development and submission comply with applicable Commonwealth management directives, procurement rules, IT policies, procedures, and security requirements. Gather, analyze, and document business and program requirements from subject matter experts, stakeholders, and organizational leadership. Facilitate regularly scheduled meetings with subject matter experts, key stakeholders, legal counsel, and other project participants. Maintain project documentation, meeting notes, action items, decision logs, and other project records throughout the procurement lifecycle. Research and document best practices from other states and recommend relevant enhancements and capabilities for consideration in the RFP. Define and document system and data security requirements in accordance with organizational policies, Commonwealth requirements, industry standards, and security best practices. Develop Service Level Agreements (SLAs), licensing requirements, security requirements, and other contractual instruments for inclusion in the RFP. Collaborate with legal counsel and stakeholders to develop SLAs and other contractual requirements for turn-key point-of-sale business processes. Develop and maintain vendor response evaluation criteria, scoring methodologies, and evaluation metrics. Assist with the evaluation of vendor proposals to ensure responses satisfy mandatory requirements and established business and technical specifications. Coordinate the compilation and response to vendor questions throughout the RFP process. Support vendor demonstrations, proposal evaluations, scoring, negotiations, and contract award activities. Provide consultation and recommendations regarding vendor scoring, selection, negotiations, and final contract award. Serve as the project advocate throughout the RFP procurement and vendor selection process. Work independently to manage project deliverables, timelines, documentation, and stakeholder coordination. Job Requirements 10+ years of experience in Project Management. 5+ years of experience drafting Service Level Agreements (SLAs). 5+ years of experience gathering requirements. 3+ years of experience preparing Requests for Proposal (RFPs). 1+ year of experience in Technical Writing. PMP Certification is highly desired. Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, United States

item.title: Director Government Affairs
item.description: Shift4 (NYSE: FOUR) is boldly redefining commerce by simplifying complex payments ecosystems across the world. As the leader in commerce-enabling technology, Shift4 powers billions of transactions annually for hundreds of thousands of businesses in virtually every industry. For more information, visit www.shift4.com. The Director, Government Affairs will lead the organization’s domestic and international government affairs strategy, serving as a key advisor to the Chief of Staff and executive leadership on legislative, regulatory, and public policy matters. This role will oversee relationships with government entities, trade associations, lobbyists, and other external stakeholders while monitoring policy developments that may impact the organization’s business and strategic objectives. The Director will develop and execute advocacy strategies, assess emerging regulatory and legislative risks and opportunities, and coordinate cross-functional efforts to ensure the organization is positioned effectively on issues of importance. This role requires strong judgment, executive presence, and the ability to navigate complex domestic and international policy environments. Key Responsibilities Develop and lead the organization’s domestic and international government affairs strategy in alignment with overall business and corporate objectives. Serve as a trusted advisor to the Chief of Staff and executive leadership on legislative, regulatory, political, and public policy developments and their potential impact on the organization. Lead relationships with trade associations, government officials, regulatory agencies, lobbyists, and other external stakeholders, representing the organization’s interests at domestic and international levels. Oversee trade association memberships and strategic participation, including evaluating opportunities, managing relationships, and ensuring the organization derives value from its external affiliations. Monitor and assess legislative and regulatory developments at the federal, state, local, and international levels, translating complex developments into clear business implications, recommendations, and action plans for leadership. Lead the coordination and oversight of external lobbyists and government affairs consultants, establishing priorities, monitoring deliverables, and evaluating effectiveness against organizational objectives. Develop and execute advocacy strategies related to key legislative and regulatory priorities, including engagement with congressional offices, government agencies, foreign governments, and multilateral organizations, as appropriate. Partner closely with Legal, Compliance, Risk, Finance, Operations, and other cross-functional teams to identify emerging policy risks and opportunities and develop coordinated organizational responses. Establish and maintain reporting dashboards and executive-level updates that communicate government affairs activities, regulatory developments, policy risks, and strategic priorities. Lead the preparation of executive briefing materials, policy positions, talking points, stakeholder maps, and other materials supporting senior leadership engagements. Build and maintain a strong network of internal and external stakeholders to proactively identify emerging issues and influence policy outcomes relevant to the organization. Provide strategic guidance on international policy matters and assess potential geopolitical, regulatory, and legislative developments that may affect the organization’s global operations. Represent the organization in relevant industry forums, conferences, trade associations, and government affairs meetings. Lead ad hoc policy research, stakeholder engagement, and strategic initiatives in support of the organization’s broader government affairs and corporate objectives. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, International Relations, Government Affairs, or a related field; advanced degree preferred. 8+ years of progressive experience in government affairs, public policy, lobbying, regulatory affairs, advocacy, or a related field, preferably within a corporate, technology, financial services, payments, or similarly regulated environment. Demonstrated experience developing and executing government affairs or public policy strategies at the domestic and/or international level. Strong understanding of legislative, regulatory, and government processes, with the ability to assess complex policy developments and translate them into actionable business recommendations. Established relationships and demonstrated experience engaging with government officials, regulatory agencies, trade associations, lobbyists, and other external stakeholders. Experience managing external government affairs consultants, lobbyists, or strategic partners. Strong executive presence and the ability to effectively advise and influence senior leaders. Exceptional communication, presentation, research, and analytical skills, with the ability to communicate complex policy matters clearly to both executive and non-technical audiences. Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities across jurisdictions and time zones. Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and operate effectively in a highly complex and evolving regulatory environment. Preferred: Experience with international policy, global regulatory affairs, trade associations, financial services or payments policy, and/or relevant professional government affairs or public policy organizations. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class.

item.title: Deputy Director Public Policy Legislative Engagement
item.description: ABOUT OUR CLIENT: Talent Road's client is a national nonprofit and field builder with the mission of improving lives by empowering students with essential skills and dispositions for making better decisions. Founded in 2014 and backed by experts in decision sciences, business, and education-including several Nobel laureates-our client believes that better decisions lead to better lives and a better society. They partner with teachers, academic and business leaders, families, and community members to raise awareness and lead the growing call to have Decision Education taught in schools nationwide. They are committed to an inclusive, supportive, and collaborative culture. Their diverse team comprises educators, researchers, subject matter experts, and other professionals dedicated to the mission. JOB OVERVIEW: The Deputy Director of Public Policy, Legislative Engagement is a senior role responsible for advancing the state and national policy agenda by coordinating legislative engagement, managing policy‑aligned outreach, and assisting with coalition and stakeholder activities that advance Decision Education. This position focuses on legislative strategy, drafting policy documents, cultivating relationships through meetings and events, state-level lobbying and advocacy, and ensuring effective communication with policymakers, external partners, and internal teams. The Deputy Director of Public Policy, Legislative Engagement will report to the Director of Public Policy (DPP) within the Public Policy Department, which is responsible for advancing state and national policy priorities to support the adoption and expansion of Decision Education. WHAT YOU WILL DO: Legislative Engagement Lead implementation of the Alliance's direct and indirect lobbying strategies in partnership with the Director of Public Policy, cultivating relationships with governors' offices, state departments of education, state boards of education, and state legislative bodies, as well as with relevant think tanks, coalitions, advocacy organizations, and trade associations. Proactively monitor, analyze, and influence key policymaker activity and legislation at the st ate and regional levels. Draft legislative memoranda, policy memoranda, and legislator education and communication materials. Translate complex federal and state education bills, administrative rules, and public budget allocations into actionable policy briefs, testimonies, and memos. Engage current and past Policymaker Fellows in the design and implementation of legislation, regulations, and pilot programs in collaboration with the Senior Manager, Public Policy. Manage relationships and contracts with retained lobbying firms in key states. Strategic Planning and Management Build regional policy, advocacy, and lobbying plans in conjunction with the Director of Public Policy, contracted lobbyists, and regional partners. Support the development and monitoring of department-level Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) related to policy development and adoption. Collaborate with the communications team, DPP, and other teams to design research briefings and public-facing toolkits that shape the national narrative around the importance of Decision Education in K-12 education policy. Support senior‑level relationship management with key strategic policy leaders, including preparation, alignment, and follow‑up for high‑value engagements. Track staff and stakeholder engagement efforts in Salesforce, Wrike, and other project management tools. Collaborate with internal teams to ensure public policy activities are aligned, supported, and communicated effectively. Design and facilitate necessary legislative training and professional development for staff and volunteers who engage in public policy opportunities and engagements. WHAT YOU NEED: At least 8 years of progressive experience leading legislative advocacy, public policy formulation, and lobbying initiatives, with a clear focus on the education sector. Deep expertise in legislative processes, state-level education governance, and public K-12 financing structures. Experience managing complex cross-sector initiatives, public policy campaigns, and education policy lobbying initiatives. Experience using a CRM system. ADDITIONAL INFORMTION: Compensation: $110,000 - $140,000 annually Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance (100% employer paid) Life Insurance (100% employer paid) Long Term Disability Insurance (100% employer paid) Employee Assistance Program 401K Retirement Plan with up to a 5% match Flexible Spending Account Up to 20 Days of Paid Time Off in your first year (prorated based on your start date) Shortened Friday workweeks and select summer months Hybrid work schedule – Office location: Bala Cynwyd, PA This position is open to both local and remote candidates. Local team members are expected to follow a hybrid schedule, working onsite at our headquarters in Bala Cynwyd, PA, on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, with remote work permitted on other business days. Fully remote employees are expected to maintain a productive home-based work environment and remain actively engaged in team operations during East Coast hours. Additionally, the role requires 30-50 percent travel, including stakeholder and legislative engagements, travel to state capitals, national conferences, and to internal and all-staff meetings at organization headquarters.

item.description: Initial Posting Date: 09/01/2026 Application Deadline: 09/22/2026 Agency: Legislative Policy & Research Committee Salary Range: $17.00 / Hour Position Type: Employee Position Title: Legislative Analyst Internship Job Description: Oregon’s nonpartisan Legislative Policy and Research Office (LPRO) seeks a highly motivated student to serve as a legislative analyst intern during the 2027 legislative session. Graduate students studying public policy, law, or a related field who are eager to learn about Oregon’s legislative process are encouraged to apply. The internship will focus on one of the following policy areas: Housing, homelessness, housing development, land use, and zoning Maternal and child health Public health, specifically substance use disorder prevention About the opportunity: The internship begins on January 4, 2027, and ends at the conclusion of the 2027 legislative session (usually near the end of June). The intern is expected to work approximately 30 hours per week in Salem. The work assigned to the intern will offer learning in committee organization and administration, bill management, research, communication, and other projects. The intern will work collaboratively with colleagues and be assigned a mentor who will provide professional growth and networking opportunities. About the office: LPRO’s mission is to provide professional, nonpartisan staffing, analysis, and research that support and inform the policymaking process. Our highest priority is to ensure that Oregon’s legislature has access to relevant and timely information on public policy issues of interest to the state. The ideal candidate: The ideal candidate for the legislative analyst internship is familiar with Oregon’s state government structure, eager to learn, and interested in pursuing a career in public policy. They enjoy working with people, are flexible and nimble in the face of change, and can serve people with different perspectives and goals. The ideal candidate is well-organized, exercises independent judgment and discretion, and has excellent written and verbal communication skills. For complete details about this internship opportunity, including the specific qualifications, please review the position description here . MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Have earned a bachelor’s degree (four-year college or university) Be a current graduate student in a master’s, PhD, JD, or professional program in public policy, public administration, law, or a field related to one of the desired policy areas: Housing, homelessness, housing development, land use, and zoning Maternal and child health Public health, specifically substance use disorder prevention OTHER REQUIREMENTS Strong desire to learn about the legislative process through hands-on experience Ability to work effectively in a nonpartisan role and serve individuals with differing political and policy perspectives KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES The successful candidate for the legislative analyst internship will have the following at the start of the internship: Knowledge of: Skill in: Computer applications, including the Microsoft suite Organizing work and keeping track of multiple complex assignments Ability to: Prioritize competing demands and meet deadlines Communicate effectively and professionally orally and in writing Maintain attention to detail Maintain confidentiality Remain nonpartisan in a highly political environment Collaborate with LPRO team members Work independently TO APPLY: Please complete the online application and upload a current resume and cover letter. In your cover letter, please share about your background and interest in public policy. You also have the option to upload a recommendation letter from your school. IF YOU ARE NOT A STATE EMPLOYEE : To apply for this position, follow the "Apply" link and complete the application & questions online. If this is your first time applying in our new system "Workday", you will need to create a new user profile. You can even drag and drop your resume into Workday and it will read and generate your Work history! Be sure to attach a cover letter, resume, and the optional recommendation letter. CURRENT STATE EMPLOYEES : Login to Workday using the Career app on your Home Page. Prior to clicking "Apply" , update your employee profile to reflect your Education, Skills, and Job History (including your current job). Attach your current cover letter, resume, and optional recommendation letter. Applications submitted without a cover letter and resume may not be considered. Please monitor your Workday account, as all communication will be sent to you through this system. You must have a valid e-mail address to apply. This announcement closes at 11:59 PM on the close date listed. SPECIAL INFORMATION: Oregon state government provides qualifying veterans and disabled veterans with preference in employment in accordance with ORS 408.225, 408.230, and 408.235. If you are requesting veterans' preference, you may receive an additional questionnaire in your Workday account. To ensure your privacy, we are asking that you complete the Veterans’ Questionnaire and attach your qualifying military documents at that time. This questionnaire will be sent to your Workday account after you submit your application. We ask that you complete the questionnaire before the application deadline; extensions may be granted if necessary and reasonable. For questions about documentation, please visit: Veterans Resources . Or call the Oregon Department of Veterans' Affairs at: 1-800-692-9666. The work experience and/or education section of your application must clearly demonstrate how you meet all the minimum and desired skills listed above. Work Authorization: The Oregon State Legislature does not offer visa sponsorships. On the first day of employment, all hires will be required to complete the US Department of Homeland Security’s Form I-9, confirming authorization to work in the United States. In addition, hires will have three business days from their first day of employment to present documents that establish employment authorization and identity. The Oregon State Legislature is an E-Verify employer and will use E-Verify to confirm that hires are authorized to work in the United States. If you have questions regarding this recruitment, or need assistance to participate in the application process, please contact Aimee Steketee, Human Resource Analyst, at aimee.steketee@oregonlegislature.gov or (503) 986-1373. The Oregon State Legislature is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to Workforce Diversity.

item.title: Lpro Legislative Analyst Fellowship
item.description: Initial Posting Date: 09/01/2026 Application Deadline: 09/22/2026 Agency: Legislative Policy & Research Committee Salary Range: $5,151 - $7,725 Position Type: Employee Position Title: LPRO Legislative Analyst Fellowship Job Description: Oregon’s nonpartisan Legislative Policy and Research Office (LPRO) seeks a recent graduate to participate in an exciting legislative analyst fellowship program. LPRO is recruiting a fellow for the 2027 calendar year . About the opportunity: LPRO offers a front-row seat to Oregon’s decision-making process. The LPRO legislative analyst fellowship is designed to provide early-career policy professionals with exposure to the state’s legislative process, experience performing the work of a nonpartisan legislative analyst, and mentorship to support professional growth. The LPRO legislative analyst fellowship is a 12-month limited-duration position beginning in January 2027. It is designed for a recent graduate of a master’s, PhD, JD, or professional program in public policy, public administration, law, or a field related to one of the following policy areas: Education Housing, homelessness, and land use Maternal and child health Public health, specifically substance use disorder prevention The work assigned to the fellow will provide a survey of the essential duties of a legislative analyst and offer learning opportunities in committee administration, workgroup management, policy research and development, and participation in internal LPRO projects. The fellow will work collaboratively with colleagues and be assigned a mentor to provide professional growth and networking opportunities. The LPRO legislative analyst fellowship allows for a hybrid work schedule. During the legislative session (January to June), the fellow will work in person in the Capitol building Monday through Friday. During the interim (July to December), the fellow will work in the office on Wednesdays and may be required to be in the office more depending on work assignments and legislative needs. About the office: LPRO’s mission is to provide professional, nonpartisan staffing, analysis, and research that support and inform the policymaking process. LPRO supports legislators, committees, and task forces with committee management, nonpartisan research, and language interpretation services. Our priority is to ensure that Oregon’s legislature has access to relevant and timely information on public policy issues of interest to the state. The ideal candidate: The ideal candidate for the LPRO legislative analyst fellowship has a background in one or more of the identified policy areas and is interested in learning about those issues in Oregon. They are familiar with Oregon’s state government structure, eager to learn, and committed to pursuing a career in public policy. They excel in a collaborative team environment, are flexible and nimble in the face of change, and can serve people with different perspectives and goals. The ideal candidate is well organized, able to exercise independent judgment and discretion, and has excellent written and verbal communication skills. The minimum qualifications, as well as the knowledge, skills, and abilities desired for this position, are below. For complete details about this fellowship opportunity, please review the position description here . MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s degree (four-year college or university) Have earned a graduate degree within five years of applying in public policy, public administration, law, or a field related to one or more of the following policy areas: Education Housing, homelessness, and land use Maternal and child health Public health, specifically substance use disorder prevention OTHER REQUIREMENTS Strong desire to learn about the legislative process through hands-on experience Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a nonpartisan role and serve individuals with differing political and policy perspectives KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES The successful candidate for the LPRO legislative analyst fellowship will have the following at the start of the fellowship: Knowledge of: At least one of the listed policy areas Oregon’s governance structure Public policymaking foundations Skill in: Computer applications, including the Microsoft suite Organizing work and keeping track of multiple complex assignments Ability to: Prioritize competing demands and meet deadlines Communicate effectively and professionally orally and in writing Maintain attention to detail Maintain confidentiality Remain nonpartisan in a highly political environment Collaborate with LPRO team members TO APPLY: IF YOU ARE NOT A STATE EMPLOYEE : To apply for this position, follow the "Apply" link and complete the application and questions online. If this is your first time applying in our new system, Workday, you will need to create a new user profile. You can even drag and drop your resume into Workday, and it will read and generate your Work History. Be sure to attach a current resume and cover letter; both are required for consideration. You may also attach a letter of recommendation from a faculty member in the graduate program from which you earned your graduate degree, although this is optional. CURRENT STATE EMPLOYEES : Login to Workday using the Career app on your Home Page. Prior to clicking "Apply" , update your employee profile to reflect your Education, Skills, and Job History (including your current job). Attach a current cover letter and resume. Applications submitted without both required documents may not be considered. You may also attach an optional letter of recommendation from a faculty member in the program from which you earned your graduate degree. Please monitor your Workday account, as all communication will be sent to you through this system. You must have a valid e-mail address to apply. This announcement closes at 11:59 PM on the close date listed. SPECIAL INFORMATION : Oregon state government provides qualifying veterans and disabled veterans with preference in employment in accordance with ORS 408.225, 408.230, and 408.235. If you are requesting veterans' preference, you may receive an additional questionnaire in your Workday account. In order to ensure your privacy, we are asking that you complete the Veterans’ Questionnaire and attach your qualifying military documents at that time. This questionnaire will be sent to your Workday account after you submit your application. We ask that you complete the questionnaire before the application deadline; extensions may be granted if necessary and reasonable. For questions about documentation, please visit: Veterans Resources . Or call the Oregon Department of Veterans' Affairs at: 1-800-692-9666. The salary in this job posting reflects the base salary without contributions to the Public Employee Retirement System (PERS). Employees eligible for PERS will have their salary increased by 6.95% and 6% will be automatically subject to a mandatory employee contribution to PERS. The work experience and/or education section of your application must clearly demonstrate how you meet all the minimum and desired skills listed above. An offer including salary will not be extended until an equal pay analysis is completed pursuant to ORS 652.220 and 659A.357. An equal pay analysis will be conducted utilizing the education and work experience section of the legislative application. item.title: Public Affairs Specialist Legislative Affairs Specialist
item.description: Duties Serves as liaison to Congress and works with the Department of Justice (DOJ), other government agencies, and non-government organizations on legislative and congressional issues. Monitors, tracks, and analyzes legislation. Works toward enactment of legislation that will have a positive impact on the BOP and the avoidance of legislation that will have a negative impact on the agency. Provides information to Members of Congress. Prepares BOP officials to testify at congressional hearings in fulfillment of Congress' role of oversight of the Executive Branch. Assists members' offices in fulfilling their responsibility to provide services to their constituents. Helps ensure the effective and timely implementation of statutory changes. Summary Corrections professionals who foster a humane and secure environment and ensure public safety by preparing individuals for successful reentry into our communities. Requirements Conditions of employment Career Transition Programs (CTAP or ICTAP) : These programs apply to Federal and/or DOJ employees who meet the definition of surplus or displaced from a position in the competitive service. To receive selection priority for this position, you must: Meet CTAP or ICTAP eligibility criteria; Be rated well-qualified for the position, scoring at least half of the total possible points for the vacancy KSAs or competencies; and Submit the appropriate documentation to support your CTAP eligibility: A copy of the agency notice (i.e., separation notice or agency RIF letter), Most recent performance appraisal, and Most recent SF-50 showing current/former position, grade, promotion potential, and duty location. See USAJOBS' Career Transition Programs for more information. EEO Statement/Policy: The United States government does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, political affiliation, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, genetic information, age, membership in an employee organization, retaliation, parental status, military service or other non-merit factor. More information can be found here: U.S Department of Justice - Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Key Requirements: Qualifications To be considered for the position, you must meet the following qualification requirements: Education: There is no substitution of education for specialized experience for this position. Experience: You must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level. To be creditable, this experience must have equipped the applicant with the particular qualifications to perform successfully the duties of the position, and must typically be in or related to the position to be filled. Some examples of this qualifying experience are: Experience that demonstrates knowledge of the structure, operations, procedures, and activities of the U.S. Congress and the process by which Federal legislation is developed, amended, and enacted. Experience which demonstrates the ability to provide a smooth and accurate flow of information between agency components, government agencies, and the public. Experience in preparing a summary of the impact of legislation, including an assessment of its effect on Federal, State and/or local corrections and criminal justice systems. Experience in preparing issue papers, talking points and other briefing material for use by executive-level officials to respond to Congressional inquiries. If applicable, credit will be given for paid and unpaid experience. To receive proper credit, you must show the actual time (such as the number of hours worked per week) spent in activities. **Your eligibility for consideration will be based on your responses to the questions in the application.** Education ONLY if education is a requirement/substitution for specialized experience, applicant MUST upload legible transcripts as verification of educational requirement. Transcripts MUST be uploaded and electronically linked from USAJOBS at the time you apply and MUST include identifying information to include School Name, Student Name, Degree and Date Awarded (if applicable). All academic degrees and coursework must be completed at a college or university that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education. For a list of schools that meet this criteria, Click Here . Foreign Education: For information regarding foreign education requirements, please see Foreign Diploma and Credit Recognition at the U.S. Department of Education website: Recognition of Foreign Qualifications . Additional information Special Conditions of Employment Section: The incumbent is subject to geographic relocation to meet the needs of the agency. Appointment is subject to satisfactory completion of a urinalysis, physical, and background investigation. All applicants are subject to National Crime Information Center (NCIC) and credit checks. Additional selections may be made if vacancies occur within the life of the certificate. This is a secondary/non-law enforcement coverage position. Individuals that DO NOT have three years of law enforcement coverage gained in a primary law enforcement position by the closing date of the vacancy announcement are ineligible for secondary law enforcement position(s) and coverage but may still be considered for a non-law enforcement position. Individuals selected who are under the Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS) or Civil Service Retirement System (CSRS) and who have not had three years "primary" law enforcement retirement coverage, will not be covered by law enforcement retirement while in this position. To regain coverage, individuals must return to a position with "primary" coverage. Current Federal Law Enforcement Employees: Completion of the mandatory courses "Introduction to Correctional Techniques (ICT) Phase I and Phase II" is a condition of employment for this secondary law enforcement position. Employees who have not yet completed ICT Phase I and II will be required to do so after entering the position. This requirement does not apply to non-law-enforcement positions. Eligibility for secondary law enforcement coverage is determined in accordance with applicable regulations. Coverage may be attained through any qualifying federal law enforcement officer service that meets the definitions in 5 U.S.C. 8401(17) and satisfies the conditions in 5 CFR 842.803. Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended that would interfere with completing the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, you will be granted the opportunity to request a RA in your online application. Requests for RA for the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments and appropriate supporting documentation for RA must be received prior to starting the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. If you meet the minimum qualifications of the position, after notification of the adjudication of your request, you will receive an email invitation to complete the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, based on your adjudication decision. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments if you received the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need a RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments . ( https://appsupport-usastaffing.opm.gov/hc/en-us/sections/45063131363475-Reasonable-Accommodation-Information ) Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. A career with the U.S. government provides employees with a comprehensive benefits package. As a federal employee, you and your family will have access to a range of benefits that are designed to make your federal career very rewarding. item.title: Visiting Assistant Professor Of Political Science
item.description: The Political Science Discipline at St. Norbert College invites applications for a visiting assistant professor position (beginning in August 2027) with a specialization in the areas of Public Law and American Government. Candidates should either be ABD or hold a Ph.D. and be enthusiastic about teaching both introductory and upper-level courses, including Courts, Constitutional Law, Civil Liberties, and introductory American Politics. The ability to teach upper-level courses in parties, elections, Congress, and/or the presidency is a plus. The position includes assisting with pre-law advisement. The teaching load is three or four courses per semester (total of seven courses per year), which typically includes introductory courses and at least one upper-division course per semester. The position is offered as a one-year contract, with the possibility of renewal contingent on a positive annual performance review and/or institutional needs. Please note that this is an on-site role requiring full-time on-campus attendance. Candidates should submit a letter of application, CV, and a teaching statement through the “Apply” link found on this page. Student and peer evaluations and syllabi are welcome. Review of applications will begin October 9 and continue until the position is filled. Candidates are asked to submit a separate 1-page statement describing how they envision contributing to and supporting the mission and values of St. Norbert College through their teaching, scholarship, and service. Candidates are highly encouraged to read the College’s Catholic , Liberal Arts , and Norbertine identity statements as well as Ex Corde Ecclesiae and address how they could participate in the educational vision laid out in these documents. Questions regarding the position should be addressed to Jamie Lynch at jamie.lynch@snc.edu or Wendy Scattergood at wendy.scattergood@snc.edu . About St. Norbert College: St. Norbert College, located on the ancestral home of the Menominee Nation, is a thriving, nationally ranked Catholic liberal arts college known for its academic excellence, global focus, and leadership and service opportunities. We acknowledge the living history and contributions of the Indigenous communities that inhabited this land prior to the establishment of St. Norbert College, as well as the sovereign Native American Nations who continue to contribute to the flourishing of our communities. Situated on an attractive, riverside campus in De Pere, Wisconsin -- a community contiguous with the city of Green Bay–St. Norbert is the only college in the world sponsored by the Norbertines, a Catholic order devoted to community, education, and serving the needs of others. St. Norbert College (SNC), a Catholic, Norbertine, and Liberal Arts College, provides an educational environment that fosters intellectual, spiritual, and personal development. As the only Norbertine institution of higher learning in the world, our roots, traditions, and commitments create a unique and enriching educational experience for our students. At SNC, our commitment to communio – the Norbertine ideal of a community united as one – is grounded in the principles of dignity, truth, and justice. Consistent with these principles, St. Norbert is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment. We seek those who will embrace our mission and commitment to building a vibrant, inclusive, and spiritually engaged community ( https://snc.edu/mission ). As one of the nation’s top Catholic liberal arts colleges, St. Norbert builds on the beliefs and practices of an ancient religious order while responding to the current needs of its students and communities. Today at St. Norbert College, the spirit of Norbert of Xanten, who founded the Norbertine order of priests in the twelfth century, lives through this modern, bustling community dedicated to transforming and empowering its students. The college has seen remarkable development in the past decade, particularly the construction and renovation of more than $150 million in campus facilities and infrastructure. At St. Norbert College, a holistic approach to students characterizes the curriculum and classroom; faculty use their award-winning research to challenge and encourage students to greater curiosity, and students learn and collaborate both in and outside the classroom in an integrated experience. St. Norbert College is organized into three academic divisions – Arts and Sciences, Health and Human Development, and the Donald J. Schneider School of Business & Economics. Exempt Scheduled Weekly Hours: 40 The duties and responsibilities listed in this job description are intended to describe the general nature and level of work that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the job if work is similar, related or a logical assignment to the job. Percentage of time may vary widely depending on the needs of the position during any particular time period. This job description does not constitute an employment agreement between the employer and employee and is subject to change by the employer as the needs of the employer and requirements of the job change.

item.title: Executive Director
item.description: Executive Director Salary: $105,000 - $115,000 commensurate with experience Location: Remote within Vermont, with significant time in Montpelier during legislative session ABOUT PUBLIC ASSETS INSTITUTE Public Assets Institute, a Vermont 501c3 nonprofit research and advocacy think tank, is seeking applications and nominations for the position of Executive Director (ED). Public Assets has achieved statewide respect and influence for its data-focused analysis, timely input on key public policy issues, alliance-building efforts, and accessible communication about complicated fiscal and economic topics. Its annual State of Working Vermont report is considered an indispensable resource and its ongoing work on education funding has been critical to Vermont having one of the most equitable school funding systems in the country. Public Assets brings an equity lens to all its work and partnerships to improve the lives of everyone in the state. For more information, visit Public Assets’ website: https://publicassets.org . THE OPPORTUNITY The next Executive Director (ED) will continue to champion Public Assets Institute's mission to improve the well-being of all people in Vermont, advance racial, social, and economic justice, and promote policies that the state government can enact. Reporting to and serving on the Board of Directors, the ED will spearhead the development and implementation of strategies and will provide leadership and oversight of Public Assets’ strategy, operations, personnel, and finances. This role is ideal for a leader who thrives at the intersection of research and policy, can navigate complex policy environments and communicate complicated tax and budget policy issues clearly, and can build meaningful relationships with funders, partners, policymakers, and communities. We envision the new ED can expect to lead in the following areas: Continue to solidify Public Assets’ sound and accessible tax, budget, and economic data and analysis to advance policies that further racial, social, and economic equity. This is the foundation of its reputation and policy impact. Working with a small team, the ED will ensure Public Assets continues to produce trusted, nonpartisan data, analysis, and testimony that legislators, coalition partners, and the public rely on. Carry a vision for how sound data and analysis reach Vermonters where they actually are to make the case for tax, budget, and economic policies that work for all. The ED will articulate policy insights and data to policymakers, funders, the media, and the public to reflect the priorities and needs of people living in Vermont. They will focus on budget, tax, and economic policies, including education funding policy, which are essential for effecting equity, sustainability, and shared prosperity. They will modernize how Public Assets tells its story, ensuring its rigorous research informs policy. Set organizational vision and strategy that explores current and new opportunities together with the Board and staff. Leading in a generative and inclusive manner, the ED will think about the shifting political landscape in Vermont to keep the organization’s strategy nimble and responsive to external trends, developments, and opportunities. In addition, the ED will ensure that the various parts of the organization are in alignment and that key projects and campaigns are on target and aligned with the organizational strategy. Strengthen the financial sustainability of the organization by building and maintaining sustained relationships with existing individual donors, Vermont funders, and national foundations and partners. In addition, the ED will seek out new opportunities for expanding the organization’s funding sources and steward all supporters of the organization through regular interactions and communications. Lead a dedicated and passionate team of staff and Board members who care deeply about the issues at hand and are effective implementers and ambassadors of Public Assets. To build upon the current organizational culture, the ED will continue to strengthen internal communication, reporting structures, performance review and professional development, project management, and benefits to support Public Assets’ healthy, high-trust culture and effectively grow leaders and delegation within the organization. CANDIDATE PROFILE The most competitive candidates will be those who can bring the following leadership to Public Assets: Translator of Research to Policy The ED will embody Public Assets values and mission to improve the well-being of all people in Vermont and advance racial, social, and economic justice through research, fiscal analysis, public engagement and policy development. They will be unafraid to challenge the status quo and reinvigorate policy debates with varied audiences, from grassroots organizers to institutional partners. The ideal candidate brings strong research and analytical skills, familiarity and comfort speaking on Public Assets' core policy areas, and working knowledge of Vermont public policy. Fundraiser for Sustainability The ED will have the character and confidence to work in a highly visible role as the chief ambassador and fundraiser for Public Assets. A successful candidate will speak credibly and knowledgeably with diverse audiences about Vermont tax, budget, and economic policy in order to champion financial and non-financial support from a broad range of constituents. The leader will work closely with the Board and staff to nurture long-standing donor relationships and cultivate new, diverse funding sources. Leader for Strategic and Operational Excellence The Executive Director will be a strategic, results-oriented leader who ensures sound financial management, governance, and day-to-day operations align with strategic goals. With a deep understanding of effective nonprofit management and an inclusive leadership philosophy, they will ensure the personal and professional development and growth of all employees and cultivate a collaborative Board while driving work forward. Champion for Racial Justice, Equity, and Inclusion Equipped with a multifaceted understanding of how racial inequity plays out in our society and in movement building, the successful candidate will have a demonstrated ability to lead the organization’s efforts to continue to integrate racial equity into all aspects of the organization’s work to address structural implications and disproportionate impacts of policies, activities, and decisions on communities depending on their race, class, ethnicity, and immigration status. QUALIFICATIONS We believe these areas of leadership will be held by someone with many of these qualifications: Ten or more years of experience working on social and economic policy issues with an emphasis on data-driven research, policy, and advocacy Five years of experience managing personnel and financial affairs of a department or organization of similar or greater size Ability to guide organizational and policy strategy and to share a compelling vision and complex information and data to various audiences Commitment to Public Assets’ values of racial justice, equity, and inclusion and to the success of Vermont’s most vulnerable communities Ability and comfort to communicate with funders, including making asks and fundraising from foundation and individual donors Effective relationship builder and collaborator, ideally with legislators and policy makers, partners, funders, and community leaders Familiarity with the Vermont policy landscape Management style grounded in collaboration, trust, and flexibility with the ability to move work and decisions forward Ability and willingness to be at the statehouse frequently during session COMPENSATION The compensation range for this position is $105,000 - $115,000 with final salary commensurate with experience. Public Assets operates with a 35-hour, full-time work week and offers many benefits, including health insurance and generous holidays, vacation time, and paid family and medical leave. TO APPLY Public Assets Institute is partnering with Callie Carroll and Ankita Jhaveri of CLC Endeavors to support this process. To apply, please submit a resume and cover letter to PAI-ED@clcendeavors.com . We encourage interested candidates to apply by October 4, 2026 , though applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis. Please note: your application will be reviewed by a person, so we appreciate your patience as we take the time to consider each set of materials. While all hiring processes are human-centered and therefore subject to change, we anticipate moving through the following steps: Preliminary screening interview with CLC Endeavors Narrative in-depth interview with CLC Endeavors Panel interview with Search Committee members Final interview with staff and Board members Public Assets Institute is an equal opportunity employer committed to inclusive hiring and dedicated to diversity in our work and staff. We seek applications from all qualified candidates and do not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices based on actual or perceived race, color, religion, national origin, ethnicity, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, uniformed service member status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law. Women, people of color, LGBTQ+ persons, and people with disabilities are encouraged to apply.

item.title: Legislative Analyst
item.description: Duties Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Serves as a Congressional Liaison and primary point of contact for legislative and congressional matters affecting Special Operations programs, policies, missions, and resources. Analyzes complex legislative, policy, authorization, and appropriations issues to assess their impact on Special Operations programs, priorities, and organizational objectives. Develops, reviews, and coordinates responses to congressional inquiries, testimony, briefing materials, information papers, legislative proposals, appeals, and other congressional correspondence. Plans and coordinates congressional engagements, hearings, briefings, and related activities with Members of Congress, congressional staff, senior Department officials, and internal and external stakeholders. Advises senior leadership on congressional and legislative matters, develops recommended courses of action and engagement strategies, and communicates organizational positions on sensitive or high-visibility issues. Summary This position resides within the Secretariat for Special Operations (SSO), Office of the Assistant Secretary of War for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict (OASW(SO/LIC)). Under 10 U.S.C. §§ 138 and 167, the ASW(SO/LIC) is the principal civilian advisor to the Secretary of War for special operations and oversees SOF readiness, resources, equipment, and civilian personnel. Requirements Conditions of employment U.S. Citizenship is required Males born after 12-31-59 must be registered or exempt from Selective Service (see https://www.sss.gov/Home/Registration) May be required to successfully complete a probationary/trial period Must be determined suitable for federal employment Required to participate in the direct deposit program This position is subject to pre-employment and random drug testing This position is subject to the DoD Priority Placement Program Incumbent must be able to obtain and maintain a TOP SECRET Security Clearance with SCI. This position may require the incumbent to work other than normal duty hours, which may include evenings, weekends and/or holidays and/or overtime This position may require occasional travel away from the normal duty station via military or commercial aircraft Relocation Incentives may be offered. Qualifications In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below. You may qualify at the GS 15 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-14 grade level in the Federal service which includes: 1. Analyzing complex legislative, congressional, defense policy, or defense program issues to determine their impact on organizational missions, programs, priorities, or resources; 2. Developing, coordinating, or reviewing legislative and congressional materials, such as responses to congressional inquiries, hearing testimony, briefing materials, legislative proposals, appeals, or information papers; AND 3. Providing authoritative advice and recommendations to senior military or civilian leadership concerning congressional actions, defense policy, authorizations, appropriations, or other legislative matters affecting organizational programs and priorities. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. All qualifications and education requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume.Your resume may not exceed two (2) pages . For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the duration of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume at https://help.usajobs.gov/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, as part of their application package, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, indicating the service member is otherwise eligible and will be discharged or released within 120 days from the date of submission.. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. This "certification" must include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable), and date any terminal leave will begin. It must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible". Members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if they are on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. Education Education cannot be substituted for experience. Additional information Probationary Periods: As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you will be required to serve a 1-year probationary period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider: - your performance and conduct; - the needs and interests of the agency; - whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and - whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service. Upon completion of your probationary period your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest. Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP): This program applies to employees who have been involuntarily separated from a Federal service position within the competitive service or Federal service employees whose positions have been deemed surplus or no longer needed. To receive selection priority for this position, you must: (1) meet ICTAP eligibility criteria; (2) be rated well-qualified for the position; and, (3) submit the appropriate documentation to support your ICTAP eligibility. For more information visit: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/workforce-restructuring/employee-guide-to-career-transition/ Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended that would interfere with completing the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, you will be granted the opportunity to request a RA in your online application. Requests for RA for the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments and appropriate supporting documentation for RA must be received prior to starting the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. If you meet the minimum qualifications of the position, after notification of the adjudication of your request, you will receive an email invitation to complete the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, based on your adjudication decision. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments if you received the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need a RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments . Reemployed Annuitants: Applicants in receipt of an annuity based on civilian employment in the Federal Service are subject to the DoD Policy on The Employment of Annuitants (DODI 1400.25, volume 300). http://www.esd.whs.mil/DD/DoD-Issuances/140025/ Nepotism : Under the provisions of 5 USC 3110, an individual may not be appointed into a position if the position is under the supervisory chain of command of a relative. Additional vacancies may be filled by this announcement. Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution.
