item.title: Public Policy Associate Pcn 047
item.description: We all face challenges and transitions in our lives, and when we do, we must be able to count on the strength of community for support. For the people of Los Angeles, Jewish Family Service LA (JFSLA) is that trusted source of support. We are a comprehensive network of services that welcomes individuals and families of all ages and identities to our full spectrum of care. Our highly trained staff and volunteers work closely with individuals and their loved ones to problem-solve and guide them on their paths to safety, security, wellness, and fulfillment. JFSLA staff share in our mission and work towards our goals with the highest level of responsibility, professionalism, and integrity. JFS demonstrates our commitment to our staff by offering a comprehensive benefits package and a nurturing environment. JFSLA is committed to cultivating and preserving a culture of inclusion and connectedness. In recruiting for our team, we seek the unique contributions that individuals can bring from all backgrounds. We strive for a diverse team in order to better serve our clients and ensure our excellence as an organization in identifying, designing and delivering solutions. Be part of our commitment and join our family. For more information on our philosophy and services, please tour our website www.jfsla.org The Public Policy Associate supports and advances Jewish Family Service LA's public policy, advocacy, and government relations initiatives. The position is responsible for conducting policy research and analysis, monitoring legislative and regulatory developments, developing advocacy materials, coordinating stakeholder engagement activities, and representing the agency in public policy forums and coalitions. The Public Policy Associate exercises independent judgment and discretion in evaluating policy issues, developing recommendations, coordinating advocacy efforts, and supporting strategic initiatives that further the mission and priorities of JFSLA. Qualifications Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university required. Degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Public Administration, Social Work, Communications, Law, or a related field preferred. Two or more years of experience in public policy, advocacy, government relations, community engagement, nonprofit administration, legislative affairs, or a related field preferred. Strong interest in social services, poverty, public policy, and social justice issues. Demonstrated ability to conduct research, analyze complex information, and prepare concise written reports and recommendations. Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills. Strong organizational, project management, and time management abilities. Ability to establish and maintain productive relationships with diverse constituencies, including government officials, community partners, volunteers, and internal stakeholders. Ability to work independently and collaboratively while exercising sound judgment and maintaining confidentiality. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint. Must successfully pass a criminal background check (Live Scan fingerprinting) prior to employment. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Public Policy and Advocacy Under the direction of the Senior Director, advance JFSLA advocacy initiatives related to agency priorities, social services, and government partnerships. Conduct research and analysis on legislative, regulatory, and funding issues impacting JFSLA programs and clients. Monitor and report on federal, state, and local legislation, public policy developments, and government funding opportunities. Draft policy briefs, fact sheets, legislative summaries, advocacy materials, letters, reports, and presentations. Develop recommendations regarding policy positions, advocacy strategies, and stakeholder engagement opportunities. Assist in implementing advocacy campaigns and community engagement efforts that support agency priorities. Government and Community Relations Maintain and cultivate effective working relationships with governmental agencies, elected officials, legislative staff, coalition partners, and community organizations. Represent JFSLA at coalition meetings, legislative briefings, community events, public forums, and other advocacy-related activities. Engage and mobilize community stakeholders, volunteers, and advocates on behalf of JFSLA clients and programs. Collaborate with internal departments to identify policy issues affecting programs, clients, and service delivery. Communications and Strategic Support Assist in the development of public policy-related communications, including newsletters, action alerts, social media content, presentations, and external communications. Prepare briefing materials, research summaries, talking points, and presentations for agency leadership, committees, and external stakeholders. Support the Senior Director in developing and implementing strategic public policy initiatives and advocacy priorities. Project Coordination and Operational Support Organize legislative briefings, stakeholder meetings, advocacy events, site visits, and community engagement activities. Manage logistics and preparations necessary to support advocacy initiatives, public policy events, and stakeholder engagement efforts. Develop and maintain legislative tracking systems, advocacy databases, stakeholder contact lists, and public policy records. Monitor advocacy activities and outcomes and prepare reports, summaries, and updates for agency leadership. Participate and represent JFSLA in coalition meetings as assigned by the Senior Director and follow up with strategic actions. Responsible for follow-up activities with governmental agencies, coalition partners, and community stakeholders to ensure timely completion of initiatives. Organize Public Policy Committee meetings, including agenda development, preparation and dissemination of materials, meeting coordination, documentation of key discussions, and tracking of action items. Assist with scheduling, travel coordination, correspondence, records management, and other operational activities that support the effective execution of the department's public policy and advocacy objectives. Exercise independent judgment in prioritizing assignments, identifying issues requiring attention, and recommending appropriate follow-up actions. Organize site visits, local briefings; travel arrangements, logistics and related administrative preparation as needed. Provide operational support to the Senior Director, including organizing public policy folders, preparing briefing materials, maintaining records and contact databases, tracking advocacy activities, processing correspondence and check requests, and other duties as assigned. Perform other related duties and special projects as assigned. Jewish Family Service is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran This position reports to the Senior Director of Public Policy and Government Relations.

item.title: Assistant Professor Of Political Science
item.description: The University of Chicago, Division of the Social Sciences, Department of Political Science invites applications for a tenure track position at the rank of assistant professor of American Politics for an initial 4 year renewable term. We welcome applications from the entire subfield of American politics. This is a full-time position with an expected start date on or after July 1, 2027. The selected candidate will pursue their own research agenda, collaborate with faculty in the Department of Political Science and other areas of the Division of the Social Sciences and University, and teach in both the undergraduate and graduate curriculum. The teaching load for tenure-track positions is typically four courses per year on the quarter system. Additional responsibilities include advising at all levels of the program, and service on departmental and university committees. This position is benefits-eligible. The University of Chicago offers a wide range of benefits programs and resources for eligible employees, including health, retirement, and paid time off. Information about the benefit offerings can be found in the Benefits Guidebook . All requirements for receipt of a PhD in a relevant field must be completed prior to the start of the appointment. We seek applicants with an ambitious research agenda yielding active and innovative scholarship. Successful applicants will contribute to the scholarly community of the department and university. They will have the ability or potential to be an excellent teacher in the university’s core curriculum, in introductory to advanced undergraduate courses in Political Science, and in graduate courses related to their area of expertise. We especially welcome applicants with a demonstrated strong commitment to teaching and advising.

item.title: Director Of Public Policy Community Relations
item.description: Description At DAP Health, we are committed to transforming lives and advancing health equity for all. As a leading nonprofit health care provider, we deliver compassionate, high-quality care to the diverse communities of the Coachella Valley and San Diego County. Our comprehensive services range from primary care to mental health, wellness programs, and beyond, with a focus on those who are most vulnerable. Joining our team means becoming part of a passionate, innovative organization dedicated to making a meaningful impact in the lives of those we serve. If you're looking for a dynamic and purpose-driven environment, we invite you to explore the opportunity to contribute to our mission. Job Summary The Director of Public Policy & Community Relations serves as a senior strategic leader advancing the mission and long-term sustainability of the health center through policy engagement, advocacy, and community partnerships. This role represents the organization with elected officials, government agencies, and community stakeholders, ensuring the health center’s priorities and the voices of the communities it serves are reflected in public policy and discourse. This is position partners with leaders to assess key policy developments and community impact information, synthesizing complex information into clear, actionable insights to support executive decision making, and effective communication with leadership, assisting in organizational wide communication. Supervisory Responsibilities: None Essential Duties/Responsibilities: Government Relations (Local, State, and Federal) Serve as a primary liaison between the health center and local, state, and federal elected officials and some regulatory agencies. Monitor and analyze legislative and regulatory developments impacting FQHCs, Medicaid, public health policy, and healthcare access. Identifies the specific priorities of DAP Health, developing and executing strategic advocacy plans to advance policy priorities. Organize and lead legislative site visits, briefings, and participation in health center advocacy days. Proactively draft policy briefs, testimony, talking points, and position statements for leadership and board members, ensuring executive leadership is prepared for meetings and community events Collaborate with national and state associations (e.g., NACHC, CPCA) on policy issues and campaigns Community Relations & Engagement Lead a strategic community engagement framework that aligns grassroot insights with organizational policy priorities, ensuring community voices meaningfully inform advocacy positions and public policy strategy Cultivates and manage high-level relationships with community-based organizations, advocacy coalitions, civic leaders, and faith-based networks to advance coordinated policy goals and systems-level change Ensure community engagement efforts are intentional, inclusive and policy relevant, moving beyond transactional outreach to sustained relationship-building and shared impact Identify and leverage strategic partnerships to influence policy outcomes, strengthen collective advocacy efforts, and address social and structural drivers in health Direct public-facing engagement initiatives including town halls, community forums, and listening sessions, that inform policy development, support narrative change, and build public will around healthcare access and equity Strategic Communication & Stakeholder Engagement Align policy, advocacy, and community engagement messaging, ensuring a cohesive narrative that advances organizational priorities and reinforces credibility with external and internal stakeholders Shape and develop high-impact policy and advocacy related content for newsletters, website updates, and social media posts related to policy work and community impact Collaborate with internal leaders to identify priority risks and opportunities, streamline the information for executive leadership and the board Provide regular executive-level and mid-level staff briefings on key and complex policy changes and advocacy opportunities Reporting & Compliance Maintain detailed records of meetings, contacts, and outcomes related to advocacy and stakeholder engagement Prepare reports and dashboards to track outreach, policy engagement outcomes, and stakeholder feedback. Ensure compliance with 501(c)(3) lobbying regulations and grant-funded advocacy efforts. Provides the Chief Transformation Officer & Chief Strategy Officer with forward-looking analysis of policy and regulatory developments, translating implications into strategic options, risk assessments, and clear recommendations to support governance and fiduciary oversight Synthesizes complex policy, regulatory, and community-impact information into concise, decision-ready briefings for the Board of Directors, highlighting risks, opportunities, and recommended actions Qualifications Required Skills/Abilities Ability to commit to health equity, community-centered advocacy, and the mission and values of FQHCs, with a demonstrated understanding of culturally responsive engagement and systems-level change Excellent verbal and written communication skills Strong organizational, analytical, and interpersonal skills Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree in public policy, public health, political science, communications, or a related field (master’s or equivalent advanced training preferred) Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience in government relations, public affairs, advocacy, or policy leadership within a non-profit, health care, public sector setting, or mission-driven organization Demonstrated expertise in healthcare policy and public systems, particularly issues affecting underserved, marginalized and historically excluded communities, including Medicaid, public health funding, and access-to-care policy Proven ability to build, manage, and sustain relationships with elected officials, regulatory agencies, coalition partners and community leaders to advance organizational policy priorities Experience working in or with Federally Qualified Health Centers or community health is strongly preferred Demonstrate capacity to lead through influence, collaborating effectively across departments and with external stakeholders in fast-paced, politically dynamic environments Working Conditions/Physical Requirements This position is on-site at a DAP Health location with the possibility of hybrid This job operates in an office setting and requires frequent times of sitting, standing, repetitive motion and talking May require occasional evening or weekend hours for community engagement or advocacy events Requires current and valid driver’s license and current personal auto insurance Able to travel to DAP Health locations, community events, including statewide and national travel when needed Ability to lift up to 24 pounds

item.title: Director Government Affairs San Diego
item.description: Work Location Orange, California Work Shift Day – 08hrs (United States of America) Why CHOC? At CHOC, we strive to be the leading destination of children’s health by providing exceptional and innovative care. We are responsible for the overall health of our community’s pediatric population in our hospitals, clinics, and practices. And because of our breadth of care, your career at CHOC can be as diverse and fulfilling as you determine. CHOC’s compensation structure, benefits offerings, and career development programs are geared to helping you achieve your professional and personal goals. Apply now to see where your career at CHOC can take you. Environmental Sustainability Statement Driven by the connection between children's health and a healthy environment, we commit to creating a healthcare model that incorporates environmental sustainability aligned with our mission to protect children's health and patient safety. Job Summary Please note that this position will be based out of San Diego, not Orange. The Director of Government Affairs is responsible for: • Maintaining active awareness of legislative issues, including proposed legislation and public policies that may impact Rady Children's Hospital San Diego, and developing and coordinating strategies to address them. • Working under the direction of the Vice President, Chief Advocacy & Public Policy Officer, and in partnership with the Rady Children’s Advocacy & Public Policy team and external policy advisors, to implement strategies that support Rady Children's Health’s San Diego advocacy agenda, including developing and executing legislative proposals that support health system priorities. • Working with internal and external partners to advocate for policies, practices and resources that advance Rady Children’s mission. • Collaborating and amplifying the voices of Rady Children’s Health clinicians and subject matter experts to inform positions and influence policy. Pay Range Minimum $133,827 Midpoint $177,320 Maximum $220,792 Rate of pay is determined by various factors, including but not limited to knowledge, skills, competencies, experience, education, as well as position requirements. Experience: · Required : Minimum of five (5) years of experience in government relations and legislative issues. Minimum 3 years of supervisory experience. · Preferred: Seven (7) years of experience in government relations and legislative issues; 2+ years of Children’s Hospital or Healthcare experience. Education: · Required: Bachelor’s Degree in Hospital Administration, Business Administration, Marketing or equivalent. · Preferred: Master’s Degree, MBA or MHA Specialized Skills: · Required: Strong conflict resolution skills. Able to relate and communicate positively, effectively, and professionally with others; provide leadership; be assertive and consistent in enforcing policies; work calmly and respond courteously when under pressure; lead, supervise, teach, and collaborate; accept direction. Able to use computer and software programs necessary to the position (e.g., Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint). Able to think critically; work independently; perform basic math and statistical functions; manage multiple assignments; compose written material; work well under pressure; problem solve; organize and prioritize workload; recall information with accuracy; pay close attention to detail. Licensure: · Required: None Work Environments - Functional Demand: Sedentary - Very light energy level Lift 10 lbs. box overhead. Lift and carry 15 lbs. Push/pull 20 lbs. cart. Physical Activity Requirements: Bending, Carry Objects, Climbing, Keyboard use/repetitive motion, Pinching/fine motor activities, Push/Pull, Reaching forward, Reaching overhead, Sitting, Squat/kneel/crawl (Squad & Knee), Standing, Talk or hear, Taste or smell, Twisting, Walking, Wrist position deviation Physical Activity Lifting Lifting (Floor to waist level) - Occasional 0-35%, Lifting (Waist level and above) - Occasional 0-35% Sensory Requirements: Color Discrimination, Depth Perception, Far Vision, Hearing, Near Vision Environment Requirements: Airborn Communicable Disease, Bloodborne Pathogens, Chemical, Dust Particular Matter, Extreme Noise Levels, Extreme Temperatures, Radiation, Uneven Surfaces or Elevations Non-Discrimination Statement: CHOC does not discriminate on the basis of age, race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, marital status, genetic information, disability, sex, gender (including pregnancy, breastfeeding, childbirth, lactation or related medical conditions), gender identity or expression, medical condition, sexual orientation, veteran status, military or uniformed service member status, or other protected characteristics in accordance with state and federal laws. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply for positions at CHOC, even if your experience doesn’t align perfectly with the listed qualifications for a particular role, as your unique experience may be a great addition to our culture for another one of our opportunities. item.title: Assistant City Attorney Legislative Services Community Protection Division
item.description: Assistant City Attorney (Legislative Services & Community Protection Division) San Diego City Attorney's Office San Diego, California, United States Full-time 17 days ago $250,000 - $295,000 USD yearly JOB INFORMATION The San Diego City Attorney's Office protects the people of San Diego by serving as chief legal counsel to the City of San Diego’s elected officials and operational departments; prosecuting and defending civil cases involving the City; and as the City’s prosecutor on behalf of the People of the State of California, by holding accountable those who commit crimes against the public health and safety and violate other local and state laws. Our municipal law firm employs over 190 lawyers and approximately 230 support staff, dedicated to providing legal services to the City of San Diego. The San Diego City Attorney’s Office has an opening for the Assistant City Attorney in the Legislative Services & Community Protection Division (previously Council and Government Services Division). The Assistant will manage three units and work closely with the Assistant City Attorneys for Litigation, Administration, and Municipal Operations Division (previously Mayoral Operations). The position reports directly to the City Attorney and is a member of the City Attorney’s Executive Team. The Legislative Services & Community Protection Division has two distinct roles: The Division provides legal support to the City Council and independent City departments. The Assistant City Attorney (ACA) serves as the liaison for the Council Offices to the City Attorney’s Office, works closely with the Council President’s Office, and provides legal support during Council meetings. The Division serves as general counsel to the Housing Authority and advises numerous departments and offices, including the City Clerk, Independent Budget Analyst, City Auditor, Office of Government Affairs, Your Safe Place – the Family Justice Center, the Office of Boards and Commissions, Redistricting Commission, and the City’s California Public Records Act administration. The ACA reviews and edits all ordinances and legal memoranda issued by the Division. The ACA may act for the City Attorney in her absence, sits at the dais with City Council to provide legal advice, and performs other related duties as assigned. The ACA also assists in developing training programs, leads or co-leads division-wide meetings, and has other managerial duties. The Division also houses the community protection work of the City Attorney’s Office, civilly prosecuting cases on behalf of the People of the State of California to hold accountable those who commit crimes against public health and safety and who violate other local and state laws. The Division includes the Office of Labor Standards and Enforcement, which administers and enforces the City’s labor standards ordinances and ensures employers and contractors comply with the law. It also includes the Housing Protection and Civil Code Enforcement Unit (HPU) dedicated to ensuring that housing in San Diego is safe, fair, and livable. HPU takes a focused approach to addressing persistent code violations, substandard rental housing conditions, unfair business practices, and situations where there may be a pattern or practice of violating the Residential Tenant Protections or the Short-Term Residential Occupancy Ordinance. The position is unclassified, at-will, and serves at the pleasure of the City Attorney. EXAMPLE OF DUTIES Responsibilities include: Overseeing the day-to-day operations of the Division; Supervising, training, and mentoring Division chiefs, deputy city attorneys, and the Office of Labor Standards and Enforcement team; Recruiting and hiring deputy city attorneys and staff; Providing procedural and strategic guidance and oversight to the Division chiefs and supervisors; Communicating with Mayor, Councilmembers, and City leadership and serving as the primary contact for Councilmembers and their staff; Supporting the Council President’s Office, City Clerk’s Office, and deputy city attorneys with Council-related matters; Overseeing weekly docket meetings and closed session docketing to review items on the City Council agenda; Sitting with the City Council during open session meetings; Drafting and implementing policies and procedures for the Division; Assigning, monitoring, and evaluating legal service requests from Council offices and departments covered by the Division; Assisting with media responses; Attending weekly Executive Team meetings; and Performing other duties as assigned. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS Applicants are required to: Be an active member in good standing with the State Bar of California with experience in municipal law and working with government officials. Licensed to practice law in the State of California. Licensed to practice law or willing to obtain a license in the United States District Court and the United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit. Possess strong analytical, research, writing, and oral presentation skills; be a practical problem-solver and team player; have good time management skills; and demonstrate effective communication and conflict resolution skills. The ideal candidate will have ten or more years of experience as a licensed attorney, proven managerial experience, some civil litigation experience, strong references, and experience working with municipalities and elected officials. Attorneys in this position must be able to travel to locations outside the office for legal proceedings or meetings. Therefore, possession of a valid California Class C driver's license and personal vehicle, or the ability to travel to various locations throughout the City in a timely manner, is required. SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION Work-life balance is important to the City Attorney’s Office. The Office generally supports telework and the position may allow for a hybrid schedule with a mix of in-office and remote work after the introductory period. Please refer to the Office's teleworking policy. Compensation and Benefits: The successful candidate’s annual salary will be based on qualifications and level of relevant experience. In addition to a competitive salary, the City of San Diego offers a comprehensive benefits package including: Participation in the City's Flexible Benefits Plan, which offers several optional benefit plans or a taxable cash option. $50,000 in City-paid life insurance. Flexible Spending Accounts. Paid annual leave (paid time off) accruing at 22 days per year for the 1st through 15th year of service. San Diego City Employees’ Retirement System (SDCERS) defined benefit (pension) plan. Voluntary Defined Contribution Plans (401(k)/457(b)). Retiree Medical Trust Plan. Holidays – Eleven paid holidays are provided annually and one Floating Holiday in a fiscal year. Long-Term Disability Income Plan. Other Miscellaneous Benefits: Free MTS transit pass. City-awarded discretionary leave (paid time off). 80 hours of paid Management Administrative Leave. Up to 8 weeks of paid Parental Leave. Paid time off for jury duty. Up to 40 hours of paid Bereavement Leave each fiscal year. Employee Assistance Program. To learn more about employee benefits, please review the Benefits Summary for Unclassified Employees . Some benefits currently offered to employees may be modified in the future. For further information, please contact the Risk Management Department at (619) 236-6600. Retirement benefits for this unclassified, unrepresented position will depend on the candidate's eligibility status (new hire, rehire, etc.). PRE-EMPLOYMENT REQUIREMENTS: Employment offers will be conditional pending the results of all screening processes applicable to the position, which may include the following: Proof of citizenship or legal right to work in the United States. Reference checks. Fingerprint checks: fingerprints will be submitted to the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the California Department of Justice for an arrest and conviction record report. Additional screening processes such as a background investigation. All these processes must be successfully completed before employment begins. Misrepresentation, falsification, or omission of pertinent facts in any step of the screening or selection process may be cause for disqualification or termination of employment. The City of San Diego is committed to a drug and alcohol-free workplace. HOW TO APPLY: The San Diego City Attorney's Office accepts online applications . To apply, select the position title of the job opportunity and click the "Apply" link. If you need assistance, please refer to our online employment application guide . To be considered for this position, applicants will need to submit the following by the closing date: San Diego City Attorney employment application, including responses to the supplemental questions. Cover letter and resume. A writing sample (no more than 5 pages; can be an excerpt of a document) that demonstrates their legal writing skills and reflects their own original work product. Following the closing date, resumes will be screened according to the qualifications outlined above. Only the most qualified candidates will be invited to interview. If a job has an extended deadline, applications will be considered during the extension period; however, a job may be filled before the extended date is reached. The interview process may be used to fill additional, future vacancies. Individuals must be able to perform the essential duties of the position with or without reasonable accommodation. If an applicant has questions or concerns related to the recruitment process or needs accommodation under the Americans with Disabilities Act, contact (619) 533-5811. The City of San Diego has an active Equal Opportunity/ADA Program for employment and strongly supports diversity in the workplace. Nothing in this job posting constitutes an express or implied contract for employment with the City of San Diego. DIVERSITY AND INCLUSIO

item.title: Legislative Regulatory Specialist
item.description: About the Firm Nielsen Merksamer is one of the nation's preeminent political law, government law, and lobbying firms, serving a national clientele on campaign, lobbying, and ethics compliance; legislative and administrative advocacy; election law; and high-stakes political and constitutional litigation. The firm is the go-to choice in California for navigating state and local government, and nationally for guidance on the complex laws governing political participation. Position Summary The Legislative & Regulatory Specialist supports the firm's lobbying and government affairs practice by monitoring legislative and regulatory activity, conducting policy research and analysis, tracking bills and rulemakings, and helping prepare clients and lobbyists for engagement with lawmakers and agencies. This role is well-suited for a detail-oriented policy professional who thrives in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment and wants hands-on exposure to the legislative and rulemaking process. Key Responsibilities Legislative & Regulatory Monitoring Track pending federal and/or state legislation, committee hearings, markups, and floor activity relevant to client interests Track and analyze legislative and executive branch hearings, identifying key takeaways and implications for clients Monitor agency rulemakings, notices of proposed rulemaking (NPRMs), public comment periods, and guidance documents Maintain and update legislative and regulatory tracking systems/databases for multiple clients Research & Analysis Draft bill summaries, regulatory analyses, hearing memos, and issue briefs Analyze the potential impact of proposed legislation or regulations on client industries Research legislator voting records, committee jurisdiction, and policy positions Client & Lobbyist Support Meet with clients to provide legislative and regulatory briefings and updates Prepare briefing materials, talking points, and leave-behinds for client meetings and Hill/agency visits Draft comment letters, testimony, and correspondence to legislators and regulators Testify before legislative committees or regulatory bodies on behalf of clients, as needed Assist in developing advocacy strategies and coalition-building materials Relationship & Event Support Assist with scheduling and staffing meetings with legislative offices and agency officials Support planning of fundraisers, briefings, and stakeholder events Build and maintain contact databases for legislative and agency staff Qualifications Required Bachelor’s degree in political science, Public Policy, Government, Law, Communications, or related field 2–5 years of experience in a legislative office (state legislature), executive/regulatory agency, trade association, advocacy organization, or lobbying/government affairs firm Strong understanding of the state legislative and regulatory process Excellent research, writing, and analytical skills Strong written and verbal communication skills, including comfort presenting to clients and speaking in formal settings (e.g., hearings, briefings) Ability to synthesize complex policy issues into clear, concise materials High attention to detail and strong organizational/project management skills Ability to manage multiple clients’ matters and deadlines simultaneously Skills & Attributes Discretion and sound judgment in handling sensitive and confidential client and political information Strong interpersonal skills and professional presence with government officials and clients Adaptability in a fast-moving, deadline-intensive environment Nonpartisan, client-service orientation Proficiency in Microsoft Office; comfort learning specialized policy-tracking and CRM tools Compensation & Benefits Salary range: $75,000–$150,000, commensurate with experience Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance 401(k) with firm match Paid time off and firm holidays Professional development and bar/license reimbursement (if applicable) Discretionary bonus. item.title: Legislative Advocate
item.description: Description California School Employees Association Legislative Advocate - Sacramento, CA We are seeking a Legislative Advocate for our Government Relations Office located in Sacramento, CA. The California School Employees Association (AFL-CIO) represents over 250,000 classified school employees who work in 750 school districts in California, making it the largest independent classified school employee union in the country. Our members are paraeducators, administrative and clerical workers, food service, bus drivers, groundskeepers, and maintenance and trades. We are dedicated to expanding the rights of classified school employees by securing benefits, pensions, protections and funding for the service they provide. Our mission is to champion the rights, dignity and welfare of working people. Our values include advocating for affordable healthcare and security for working families. If you feel passionate about the work we do, we want you to join us. Class specifications are intended to present a descriptive list of the range of duties performed by employees in the class. Specifications are not intended to reflect all duties performed within the job. DEFINITION To perform a variety of advanced level professional duties involved in representing the Association as a lobbyist and legislative advocate to State Legislature and Executive agencies of the State Government; to participate in legislative and political campaigns and grassroots programs as directed; and to represent the Association's legislative and political interests before organizations, the media, and school personnel. SUPERVISION RECEIVED Receives direction from the Director, Governmental Relations and the Assistant Director, Governmental Relations. EXAMPLES OF IMPORTANT RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES -- Important responsibilities and duties may include, but are not limited to, the following: Develop legislative posture on bills before the legislature; review bills before the legislature; recommend or reject bill for approval or rejection by the membership of the Association; provide testimony to legislative, budgetary and administrative hearings. Analyze state education budgets; identify and develop budget issues affecting classified employees; interpret the impact of budget and other legislation on classified employees. Research, analyze, draft and lobby for all Association sponsored legislation. Participate in legislative and political campaigns and grassroots programs as directed. Meet with Senate and Assembly committees, Senators, Assembly members, staff and with Governor's office to develop support or opposition to legislation. Negotiate with diverse special interest groups, legislative groups and administrative groups to reach compromises. Attend and participate in press conferences, media events, rallies and related events as directed. Represent the Association on various boards, committees, taskforces, and the like as directed. Stay current with new trends, innovations, current events, and laws impacting the Association or its members. Stay current with all proposed and introduced legislation, Executive Orders, state agency regulatory action, and the like affecting schools and/or school employees; notify field staff of current legislative issues/events. Participate in the development of Association communications including governmental relations monthly report, legislative report, legislative alert, bulletins and action plans. Interview, evaluate, and recommend Association endorsements for State Senate, State Assembly, State Constitutional Officers, and Congressional candidates as directed. Assist in planning and conducting staff training. Participate in the Association’s political campaigns. Consult with Director, Governmental Relations and Assistant Director, Governmental Relations as required on Association Governmental Relations matters; keep Director, Governmental Relations and the Assistant Director, Governmental Relations informed of the overall performance and results for the activities and matters of particular interest and importance. Assist with Fair Political Practices Commission (FPPC) quarterly reporting requirements and ensure all advocacy activities comply with the law and FPPC regulations. Provide responsible staff assistance to the Director, Governmental Relations and Assistant Director, Governmental Relations; prepare and present staff reports and other necessary correspondence. Attend fundraisers for Association endorsed candidates as needed. Perform related duties and responsibilities as required. QUALIFICATIONS Knowledge of: Pertinent Federal, State, and local laws, codes and regulations including funding formulas, revenue sources and general purpose. FPPC lobbyist ethics and the legislatures’ lobbyist code of conduct. Current and pending legislation and court decisions relating to the rights and obligations of Association members, leaders and staff. Principles and procedures of the legislative process including committee structure, roles and procedures. Principles, procedures and techniques of legislative advocacy. Theories, principles, and practices of collective bargaining and dispute resolution. Negotiating theory, tactics and alternative styles and processes for reaching agreement in interest disputes. Current and historical trends in the administration of institutions of primary, secondary and post-secondary public education. School district budgeting principles. History, mission, functions, and goals of the Association and of the American Labor Movement. Principles, procedures and techniques of research and investigation. English usage, style, vocabulary and syntax. Principles of mathematical and statistical computations. Political organizing and campaigning. Ability to: Prepare clear and concise reports. Analyze problems, identify alternative solutions, project consequences of proposed actions and implement recommendations in support of goals. Respond to and resolve difficult and sensitive inquiries and complaints. Demonstrate initiative, creativity and exercise independent judgment in the performance of duties. Remain calm and think clearly under pressure. Research, analyze, and evaluate information. Interpret and apply Federal, State and local policies, procedures, laws and regulations. Evaluate the political situation quickly and accurately. Effectively negotiate with legislators. Develop and prepare effective legislation for the Association. Operate effectively as a legislative advocate for the Association. Provide leadership and guidance in the development and execution of the Association's legislative program and political activities. Apply knowledge of public employee labor relations law, the legislative process, and school finance effectively in a variety of situations. Present, represent and interpret Association policy, procedures, and programs to the legislature, member-ship and staff. Recruit, train and motivate volunteers and coordinate election campaign tasks. Communicate clearly and concisely, both orally and in writing. Establish and maintain effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work. May be required to register as a lobbyist with the Secretary of State. Experience and Training Guidelines Any combination of experience and training that would likely provide the required knowledge and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain the knowledge and abilities would be: Experience: Four years of increasingly responsible experience as an advocate, preferably a legislative advocate before government entities at the state level, and representing public employees. Training: Equivalent to a Bachelors degree from an accredited college or university with major course work in business administration, political science, law, public administration or related field. License or Certificate: Possession of a valid California Motor Vehicle Operator’s license. The salary range for the Legislative Advocate is $96,777 - $140,780. Starting salaries are typically at the first step on our salary range. Consideration may be given for exceptional qualifications and experience. We offer 19 paid holidays, 3 weeks vacation to start and 5 weeks after 7 years, medical benefits for you and your family, life insurance coverage and a pension plan. To Apply Go to www.csea.com/careers , upload your resume and write a cover letter that tells us why this ad caught your eye and why we should hire you as our next Legislative Advocate! Only applications on our website will be considered. Questions? Contact HR at HREmail@csea.com . Please do not send resumes or other documents to this email. CSEA is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, committed to building and supporting a diverse workforce. This is an exempt position under the Fair Labor Standards Act. EOE/AA

item.title: Deputy Director Of Government Affairs Hybrid Sacramento Ca
item.description: Association’s Mission: California Primary Care Association's (CPCA's) mission is to lead and position community clinics, health centers and networks through advocacy, education, and services as key players in the health care delivery system to improve the health status of their communities. Purpose of the Position: CPCA and its affiliate, CPCA Advocates (Advocates), are statewide leaders in advancing policies that support community health centers, expand access to care, promote health equity, and strengthen California's health care delivery system. The Deputy Director of Government Affairs helps position CPCA and Advocates as leading voices on health care policy before the California Legislature and Administration. This position plays an active role in legislative and budget advocacy efforts by analyzing policy proposals, developing advocacy strategies, communicating legislative priorities to policymakers and members, building and maintaining strategic relationships, participating in coalitions, and representing Advocates before legislative and budget committees. The Deputy Director also supports the development of CPCA's legislative priorities, public policy principles, and advocacy initiatives that advance community health centers and health equity throughout California. Primary Responsibilities: Legislative Advocacy & Policy Research, analyze, and track legislative and regulatory proposals affecting community health centers, health care access, and CPCA policy priorities. Assess proposed legislation and regulations, develop recommendations consistent with CPCA policy, and support the development and implementation of legislative and budget advocacy strategies. Draft position letters, legislative correspondence, talking points, testimony, and other advocacy materials. Represent Advocates at legislative and budget hearings and communicate timely legislative and regulatory updates to CPCA leadership, members, committees, and stakeholders. Support the development of CPCA's public policy principles and legislative priorities. Legislative & Government Relationships Develop and maintain effective working relationships with legislators, legislative staff, state officials, CPCA leaders, members, and other government affairs stakeholders. Meet with legislators and legislative staff to communicate CPCA priorities and advocate for policy positions. Develop expertise in assigned policy areas and serve as a resource to CPCA staff and members. Coalition Building & Advocacy Strategy Develop and maintain coalitions and strategic partnerships in support of CPCA legislative priorities. Coordinate advocacy strategies with coalition partners and identify opportunities to advance CPCA policy priorities. Collaborate with advocacy, communications, grassroots, and policy partners to support legislative and advocacy efforts. Member & Internal Engagement Communicate legislative and regulatory developments to CPCA members, committees, and other stakeholders through written materials, presentations, meetings, and other forums. Staff CPCA committees, workgroups, task forces, peer networks, and other governance bodies as assigned. Collaborate with CPCA departments to support advocacy, communications, grassroots engagement, and organizational alignment. Organizational Leadership Engage in Advocates activities in collaboration with the Vice President of Government Affairs and the Director of Government Affairs and Political Engagement. Manage multiple legislative and policy assignments while meeting deadlines in a fast-moving legislative environment. Take ownership of assigned policy areas and progressively develop independent expertise and responsibility. Additional Responsibilities: Support the Association’s Strategic Plan Respond promptly and thoroughly to member inquiries. Assist with grant and budget management, contract development and reporting. Serve as lead staff to designated peer networks, work groups, task forces and committees. Serve as a subject‑matter resource, providing guidance and sharing expertise with team members. High levels of interaction with association members, vendors, and strategic partners. Travel for national and regional meetings, trainings, and site visits by air and ground transportation, as required. Report regularly to supervisor. Skills and Abilities Required: Ability to quickly understand complex legislative and policy issues and communicate their importance clearly and persuasively. Strong written and oral communication skills. Ability to develop and maintain effective professional relationships for advocacy purposes. Ability to manage multiple assignments with minimal supervision. Strong problem-solving, critical-thinking, organizational, and time-management skills. Ability to work collaboratively with senior leadership and multidisciplinary teams. Strong interpersonal and professional skills when engaging with Association members, the Board of Directors, vendors, partners, legislators, legislative staff, and government officials. Ability to develop a high level of expertise in assigned policy areas and provide guidance and technical assistance to CPCA staff and members. Proficiency in Microsoft Office and web-based applications and platforms. Education and Experience: Bachelor's degree and a minimum of five years of experience in legislative affairs, government relations, public policy, advocacy, political engagement, public affairs, or a related field. Relevant experience may be substituted for the degree requirement. Preferred Experience: Experience working with the California Legislature or California state government. Experience in California healthcare policy and an understanding of the impact of federal policy on healthcare issues. Experience with community health centers, membership associations, or nonprofit organizations is also preferred. Compensation : $118,959 - $125,957 Why You’ll Love Working Here: Hybrid work schedule (2 days in the office weekly, with an additional in-office day once per month) 100% employer-paid medical, dental, vision, life, and AD&D insurance 5% employer retirement contribution Generous paid time off: 15 vacation days, 12 sick days, 2 floating holidays, plus 18 paid holidays (including a December 24th - January 1st Winter Break) Monthly stipends: $50 for cell phone and $50 for internet Parking benefits Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and voluntary benefits, including pet insurance, Aflac, and FSA options Association Expectation: Due to network security and hybrid work this position requires the employee to have a cell phone with a data plan and home internet service, both are reimbursed at a set rate each month. All hires are required to maintain residence in California. This is a hybrid position with employees coming into the office in downtown Sacramento. Physical Demands: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Hearing and speaking to exchange information Operating a computer and other office productivity equipment Seeing to read a variety of materials Bending at the waist, kneeling, or crouching Sitting or standing for extended periods of time Lifting objects up to 30 pounds Close vision and ability to adjust focus Work Environment: Noise level is generally moderate, but at times can be noisy Meetings conducted in a Zoom or office setting Indoor varying temperature Employee must have available transportation and be able to commute into office Equal Opportunity Employment: CPCA’s workforce strives to represent California’s population, while also meeting the highest standards and qualifications of our industry.

item.title: Region Vp Public Policy And Government Relations California
item.description: As our Region VP, Public Policy and Government Relations, you will work in concert with regional presidents and relevant system leadership to shape and lead the development and implementation of advocacy and public policy initiatives with governmental branches. You will serve as a primary liaison with government officials. Every day, you will coordinate appropriate stakeholders internally and externally to facilitate attainment of the organization's public policy goals. This role requires balancing an array of high visibility responsibilities under continuous time and performance pressures, involving strategic engagement, legislative analysis, and effective communication to advance the organization's interests and mission within the complex political landscape. To be successful in this role, you will bring strong public policy and advocacy experience, exceptional relationship-building skills, and the ability to influence across government, healthcare, and executive leadership. You will be comfortable navigating complex and sensitive issues, communicating effectively with senior stakeholders, and moving between high-level strategy and hands-on advocacy. Knowledge of California’s legislative environment and healthcare policy landscape will position you for success. Develop and maintain relationships with senior government and elected officials. Builds strategic partnerships statewide to promote Dignity Health’s advocacy agenda Identify, track and develop advocacy strategies on California legislative measures, including leading and engaging hospital-level policy advocacy liaisons (PALs) on grassroots advocacy. Analyze and determine system positions on California legislation and regulatory proposals. Creates and manages testimony and submits comment letters on CA issues important to the mission. Serve as lead contact with the California Hospital Association, the Alliance of Catholic Health Care and PEACH; share operational impacts and influence policy positions and strategies.

item.title: Legislative Director Ca
item.description: Legislative Director, CA Common Cause Sacramento, California, United States Full-time 21 days ago $100,786 - $116,699 USD yearly We are looking for a Legislative Director to set the vision for and manage the legislative portfolio for Common Cause in California. This is an exciting opportunity for someone with strong collaboration and policy skills who can join us to lead our work at the State Capitol. This role will work closely with the State Director as well as teammates, board members, and partners, and will build relationships to be our ambassador at the State Capitol. This role will work to advance our policy agenda at the state capitol so that we are building a more inclusive, equitable, representative, and trustworthy democracy in our state. This is a full-time role reporting to the State Director and based in the Greater Sacramento Area, with an expectation to travel to the California State Capitol at least 3 days per week (up to 5 times per week during legislative session). We hope our new Legislative Director will start in October. Responsibilities Set the strategic direction for and advance our California and national policy agenda Manage all aspects of the legislative process for Common Cause in California, including developing ideas for and drafting legislation, determining strategies to advocate for legislation, finding bill authors, lobbying, testifying at legislative hearings, and negotiating amendments Advance our legislative agenda through coalition building and stakeholder engagement Build and lead coalitions of civil rights, tech/AI, civic engagement, and community-based organizations from across the state, and act as a representative at the Capitol for our work with these organizations Lead coalition meetings, manage cross-sector relationships, and represent Common Cause in external policy discussions, public forums, and legislative hearings Coordinate efforts with coalition partners on joint advocacy strategies, including lobbying campaigns, grassroots mobilization, and media outreach Act as a spokesperson for Common Cause, delivering testimony, making public statements, and representing the organization in high-level meetings and legislative events Drive campaigns and our advocacy strategy Lead legislative advocacy campaigns, including creating policy proposals, drafting position papers, providing testimony, and organizing strategic outreach efforts to support legislative action Communicate about our work Write op-eds, research reports, legislative factsheets, policy briefs, and memos Support our Fundraising and State Advisory Board management Administrative and Other Duties Complete administrative tasks as required, including logistics for legislative advocacy activities, stakeholder engagement, and coalition meetings. Qualifications You will thrive in this role if you have: An ability to build rapport, trust, and credibility with multiple stakeholders with diverse interests, with a track record of working collaboratively with others, navigating organizational and power dynamics to meet common goals, and respectfully navigating conflict while maintaining your values Ability to manage and meet deadlines for multiple short- and long-term priorities at once, with high attention to detail; strong organizational skills, and the ability to manage your time independently Ability to compel action through both written and verbal communication, including distilling complex concepts for a broad audience, and to differentiate communications as needed for various audiences; ideally, you have experience speaking to the press on complex issues The following is required: Strong knowledge of current issues, challenges, and opportunities related to at least one of our issue areas: Civil Rights & Civil Liberties or Anti-Corruption & Accountability; ideally, you also have knowledge of issues related to Media & Technology (in particular, AI and democracy) and/or Voting & Fair Representation Have led successful local- or state-level public advocacy campaigns related to democracy, elections, voting rights, and civil rights Willing to have a social media presence on behalf of Common Cause, including being tagged on posts and creating content on behalf of the organization (as needed, Common Cause may provide accounts for staff members to use) Ability to work in-person in Sacramento at least 3 days per week, and up to 5 days per week during legislative sessions, conferences, gatherings, and election protection work Per our nonpartisan policy, Common Cause staff members may not currently be in elected office (or running for office); on the Steering Committee or Finance Committee for any political candidate, or affiliated with the leadership of a political party Additional information about this role: $100,786 - $116,699 a year Note that we do have geography-specific percentage increases, depending on where you are located; details here . In order to ensure greater equity and transparency as an organization, Common Cause sets salary ranges consistently based on job responsibilities, and we determine salary for each staff member based on relevant years of experience (you can read more about our approach to compensation here , including where we offer geographical adjustments). For these reasons, we do not negotiate on our salary ranges or our specific salary offers. In addition to salary, we also offer a generous benefits package, including: Common Cause is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants of any race, creed, color, religion, ethnicity, national origin, income class, political affiliation, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, veteran status, or marital status, as well as applicants who have been previously incarcerated. Common Cause (501(c)(4)) and Common Cause Education Fund (501(c)(3)) are nonpartisan, nonprofit grassroots affiliate organizations dedicated to upholding the core values of American democracy. We work to create an open, honest, and accountable government that serves the public interest; promote equal rights, opportunity, and representation for all; and empower all people to make their voices heard in the political process. Founded in 1970 and headquartered in Washington, DC, Common Cause has members and supporters living in every congressional district in the United States, and offices in 23 states around the country. Sacramento, California, United States $100,786 - $116,699 USD yearly

item.title: Nysut Regional Political Organizer
item.description: Overview The Regional Political Organizer is primarily responsible for engaging NYSUT’s members and strengthening Locals in NYSUT’s Legislative and Political Action objectives. The position reports to and works under the direct supervision of the Political Director. Primary Responsibilities Mobilize and educate NYSUT members around political issues, legislative and electoral campaigns. Develop and execute new strategies to engage members Organize and track member voter registration and turnout in electoral campaigns, utilizing technology when appropriate. Educate and engage members around PAC Fundraising (Vote-Cope) Campaigns. Coordinate objectives and Campaigns with NYSUT PAC, Vote-Cope Coordinators, Regional Staff Directors (RSD), Labor Relations Specialists (LRS), Legislative Representatives, Board Members and Local Presidents. Facilitate Regional Political Action Teams. Together with PAC Coordinators plan and execute member mobilization activities in support of NYSUT endorsed candidates, legislation and issue campaigns. Recruit and prepare members to speak at press events on behalf of the Union at legislative hearings, electoral campaign events and other political activities. Help manage in-district lobbying activities, recruit and train members to attend meetings with their elected officials, attend meetings with NYSUT members. Establish and maintain relationships, lead in coalition building with community groups on behalf of the union. Raise Leader awareness of existing NYSUT programs and materials as readily available resources to engage members. Recruit and train NYSUT members to run for elected office as part of NYSUT’s Candidate Pipeline Training. Other duties and responsibilities as assigned. Qualifications A strong and proven background in union organizing, progressive politics and or political campaigns with an emphasis on field organizing. Must be able to plan and manage multiple campaigns and projects with the ability to adjust to changing priorities and strategies Bachelor’s Degree in Labor Studies /Political Science or 5+ years Union or Political Organizing experience preferred Travel as needed. Long hours including weekends and evenings are required to meet the demands of the position especially during electoral campaigns. Must possess solid verbal communication, writing and Social Media expertise Experience with event turnout, volunteer recruitment and mobilization Familiarity with the Voter Action Network (VAN), the Action Network, or other similar platforms plus. Knowledgeable of contemporary political, legislative and labor issues and current events including electoral districts and Representatives. Familiarity with the Regional Healthcare and Education. Solid computer skills including Microsoft Office. Knowledge of and a commitment to the American Labor Movement NYSUT- Who are we? NYSUT is a statewide labor organization affiliated with more than 1,200 local unions, each representing its own members. NYSUT is affiliated with two national unions, the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) and the National Education Association (NEA). NYSUT represents nearly 700,000 people who work in, or are retired from, New York's schools, colleges, and healthcare facilities, including teachers, teacher aides and assistants, college and university faculty and professional staff, school bus drivers, custodians, secretaries, cafeteria workers, nurses, and other healthcare professionals. NYSUT’s policy is to ensure an equal employment opportunity to all persons without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, age, sex, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other characteristic protected by the law. NYSUT is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. NYSUT is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. Women, people of color, and LGBTQ+ people are encouraged to apply. At NYSUT, we believe in creating a work environment free of barriers and bias, where individual outlooks and talents are respected and valued. Why Should You Apply? Competitive salary and excellent benefits, including comprehensive medical and dental insurance plans, life and long-term disability plans, and retirement plans Generous PTO plan Work-life balance Collaborative and supportive work environment with a diverse group of experienced professionals Opportunity to work in a highly respected organization, make a meaningful difference in the lives of working people, and be a proud part of the labor movement at the local, state, and national levels. How to Apply: Interested applicants should submit a cover letter and resume to hr@nysut.org by September 25, 2026

item.title: Ballot Processing Junior Clerk San Francisco Department Of Elections 1402 Junior Clerk
item.description: Ballot Processing Junior Clerk – San Francisco Department of Elections (1402 Junior Clerk) City and County of San Francisco San Francisco, California, United States Full-time 23 days ago Department Background The mission of the Department of Elections (Department) is to provide equitable access to voting and election-related services and to conduct free, fair, and functional elections for the City and County of San Francisco. Department staff work year-round to ensure that every eligible San Franciscan has easy access to safe, barrier-free registration and voting options. The Department also works continuously to improve its elections programs with the goal of making them ever more efficient and responsive to the needs of San Francisco voters. The Department strives to cultivate a workplace environment in which employees of all racial and ethnic backgrounds feel respected, valued, and supported in providing the fairest and most effective services possible to San Francisco residents. The Department is committed to maintaining an inclusive workplace and to providing the training and resources necessary for all employees to succeed in delivering equitable services to city residents. The Department is committed to reaching job seekers of all backgrounds. Everyone, including job seekers from underrepresented communities, is strongly encouraged to apply. Position Description In preparation for the November 3, 2026, Consolidated General Election, the Department is seeking applications for seasonal positions as Ballot Processing Junior Clerks (1402 Junior Clerk) to assist the Ballot Distribution division with various ballot-processing tasks. Vote-by-mail ballot processing consists of several steps, including envelope scanning, signature comparison, ballot extraction, and backfolding. Under immediate supervision, employees in these positions perform a variety of basic clerical and ballot-processing tasks using established procedures and instructions. Depending on operational needs, employees may be assigned to different ballot-processing functions throughout the assignment, including ballot sorting, backfolding, extraction, preparation for tabulation, and supporting ballot adjudication by serving as a verifier/reader alongside staff responsible for adjudicating ballots. In addition to the range of duties assigned to the 1402 Junior Clerk classification, https://careers.sf.gov/classifications/?classCode=1402&setId=COMMN , employees in these positions may perform the following essential duties and responsibilities: Perform ballot sorting, backfolding, extraction, and other ballot-preparation tasks according to established procedures. Open and process vote-by-mail and provisional ballot envelopes according to established procedures. Prepare and organize ballots for scanning and tabulation. Assist with ballot adjudication as a verifier/reader, using established procedures and instructions. Assist with the movement and organization of ballots between designated processing areas according to established procedures. Maintain routine processing counts, logs, labels, and other basic documentation as instructed. Sort and organize vote-by-mail envelopes and other election materials for processing or record retention. Organize, assemble, stage, and distribute ballots, election supplies, and other materials as directed. Perform other basic clerical, ballot-processing, and post-election tasks as assigned based on operational needs. Applicants are encouraged to learn more about what to expect during employment with the Department by watching this video: https://youtu.be/qgH-4bgAMLs . Position Schedule, Requirements, and Work Location Employees hired for this position may have different start dates based on the Department's operational needs, with tentative start dates ranging from October 30 through November 5, 2026. The Department is committed to reaching job seekers of all backgrounds. Everyone, including job seekers from underrepresented communities, is strongly encouraged to apply. Position Description: In preparation for the November 3, 2026, Consolidated General Election, the Department is seeking applications for seasonal positions as Ballot Retriever Drivers (1402 Junior Clerk). Under immediate supervision, employees in these positions perform driving, ballot retrieval, transportation, and basic clerical duties in support of the Department's ballot retrieval operations. Ballot Retriever Drivers travel to assigned ballot drop box locations throughout San Francisco to retrieve voted ballots and securely transport them to designated Department facilities according to established procedures and assigned routes. Employees work in teams and work with San Francisco Deputy Sheriffs who provide security during ballot retrieval. Employees are responsible for safely operating assigned City vehicles, following assigned routes and retrieval instructions, handling and transporting ballots according to established chain-of-custody procedures, using smartphones for navigation and communication, and completing required retrieval records and documentation. Employees also visually inspect assigned ballot drop boxes and surrounding areas for observable damage, tampering, obstructions, or other issues and document and report observed conditions to the Ballot Retrieval Operations Clerk or supervisor. Employees may perform routine cleaning or minor upkeep of ballot drop boxes as specifically directed. In addition to the range of duties assigned to the 1402 Junior Clerk classification ( 1402-Junior Clerk | City and County of San Francisco ), employees in these positions may perform the following essential duties and responsibilities: Retrieve voted ballots from assigned ballot drop box locations according to established collection and chain-of-custody procedures. Safely operate an assigned City vehicle to travel between designated ballot drop box locations and transport retrieved ballots to designated Department facilities. Follow assigned routes, schedules, and instructions provided for each ballot retrieval assignment. Handle, secure, and transport retrieved ballots according to established chain-of-custody and ballot security procedures. Complete required ballot retrieval logs, chain-of-custody forms, and other routine documentation according to established procedures. Visually inspect assigned ballot drop boxes and surrounding areas for observable damage, tampering, obstructions, or other conditions requiring attention. Photograph, document, and promptly report observed ballot drop box conditions or other issues to designated Department staff according to established procedures. Perform routine cleaning or minor upkeep of ballot drop boxes as directed. Use a smartphone and navigation applications to locate assigned ballot drop boxes and communicate with Department staff while in the field. Load, unload, carry, and move ballot containers, election materials, and supplies associated with assigned retrieval duties. Promptly report delays, vehicle issues, retrieval issues, or other circumstances affecting the assigned route to designated Department staff. Work cooperatively with assigned team members and San Francisco Deputy Sheriffs during ballot retrieval operations. Assist with Voting Center line management, polling place support, Poll Worker Dispatch operations, or other Election Day assignments as needed. Perform other basic clerical, election-related, and post-election tasks as assigned based on operational needs. City vehicles, phones, official badges, and safety vests will be provided. Position Schedule, Requirements , and Work Location Employees hired for this position may have different start dates based on the Department's operational needs, with tentative start dates ranging from October 20 through October 28, 2026. The tentative end date will be between November 4 and November 13, 2026. Actual start and end dates will depend on the Department's operational needs. Work will primarily be performed in the field at ballot drop box locations and other election-related locations throughout San Francisco. Employees will report to City Hall to receive assignments, vehicles, equipment, and other materials as directed. Training and Assignment Schedule: The following mandatory paid training will be provided: In-person training covering defensive driving and City vehicle requirements. In-person training covering ballot retrieval duties, ballot security, and chain-of-custody procedures. In-person vehicle and route-driving training. On-site training covering ballot drop box procedures, ballot removal, inspection, routine cleaning, and minor upkeep. Employees will be assigned ballot retrieval routes and schedules based on operational needs. Election Day, November 3, 2026, will involve an extended work assignment, and employees must be available to work until assigned ballot retrieval operations are completed. Work hours will vary based on the demands of the election cycle and may range from 20 to 40 hours per week. Candidates must be available to work flexible schedules, including early mornings, evenings, weekends, Election Day, and overtime, as required by operational needs. Overtime hours are paid at 1.5 times the regular hourly rate. Work will involve extensive driving throughout San Francisco, frequent entry into and exit from an assigned vehicle, and repeated loading, unloading, lifting, and carrying of ballot containers and related materials. Employees must be comfortable driving for extended periods while safely navigating City streets and completing assigned retrieval routes. The position requires prolonged periods of sitting while driving, frequent use of hands and arms while handling ballot containers and materials, and the ability to lift and handle items weighing up to 50 pounds. This is a temporary exempt as-needed position. Temporary exempt as-needed employees who have worked more than 1040 hours in any consecutive 12-month period, and whose normal work week at the time of inclusion in the system is not less than 20 hours are eligible for health coverage and retirement benefits. For more information on the City and County of San Francisco benefit policies, refer to the Department of Human Resources website at https://careers.sf.gov/benefits/ . Position Salary: $29.55 per hour Minimum Qualifications: Experience: Six (6) months of clerical experience including preparing and maintaining a variety of records and/or documents, filing, use of office equipment, public contact and processing of incoming and outgoing mail. Substitution: Any one of the following may substitute for the required experience: Completion of 15 semester units (or equivalent quarter units) of coursework from an accredited college or university; OR Completion of a clerical training program (240 hours); OR Completion of an approved City and County of San Francisco Clerical Administrative Training program. Desired Qualifications The ideal candidate will have: Experience driving and parking regularly throughout San Francisco. Strong knowledge of San Francisco streets and neighborhoods or demonstrated ability to navigate efficiently using navigation applications. Ability to follow written and verbal instructions, assigned routes, retrieval schedules, and chain-of-custody procedures accurately. Strong attention to detail and ability to accurately complete routine logs, forms, and other required documentation. Ability to work independently in the field and cooperatively with an assigned team member while maintaining regular communication with Department staff. Dependability, punctuality, and a strong commitment to ballot security and safe driving. Ability to remain attentive and organized while completing repetitive retrieval assignments and working extended hours. Experience using smartphones, navigation applications, and electronic forms. Ability to work effectively and professionally with Department staff, assigned team members, San Francisco Deputy Sheriffs, and members of the public. Basic knowledge of how to respond to common vehicle issues, such as a dead battery or flat tire. Additional Requirements Because driving and the physical retrieval of ballots are essential functions of this assignment, applicants must: Have a valid California driver's license and a driving record that meets the requirements below. Have no more than 2 points within the last 3 years and no more than 1 point within the last year. Have no DUI, reckless driving, or endangerment violations within the last 10 years. Be comfortable safely operating a minivan, cargo van, or other assigned City vehicle for extended periods throughout San Francisco. Voter Guides assist voters in navigating the Voting Center, assess the services being requested and direct voters to the appropriate service area or process, respond to questions regarding voting services and procedures, and resolve routine voter-service issues by applying established Department procedures and guidelines. Employees in these positions must learn and apply election-related procedures and information in a short period of time and communicate that information clearly and accurately to voters. Voter Guides are expected to exercise judgment in applying established procedures to varying voter circumstances, determine the appropriate response within established guidelines, and recognize matters that require referral to designated staff. The position requires strong customer service and interpersonal skills and the ability to remain attentive, patient, and professional while assisting a high volume of voters in a fast-paced public environment. Manage voter flow and lines within and around the Voting Center to support orderly and efficient operations. Explain Voting Center processes, requirements, and available voting services to voters and provide instructions appropriate to the voter's circumstances.
